# authwit-lifecycle-and-execution-followups

Make the authwit lifecycle (grant → consume → revoke → registry toggle) testable — by machine (network e2e) and by hand (playground panel) — and batch the small execution-arc follow-ups recorded on PR #83. Tier: **mid**.

## Why now

- `revokeAuthwits` + `setRegistryEnabled` (`auth-registry/service.ts:93,149`) call `executeSendTransaction` directly and have ZERO e2e coverage — manual QA is their only behavioral gate today (execution-decomposition resolved Ask A4; codex post-impl MED finding).
- Nothing in the repo can CONSUME an authwit, so revoke can't be proven to work: the playground grants (`sections/authwit.ts` — createAuthWit callIntent/innerHash) but never consumes.
- Three small follow-ups from PR #83 are ledgered and cheap to batch: cancelJob ownership, `dapp_execute` start-path unification, `E2E_REQUIRE_SETUP` node-health gap.

## Approved scope (Phase 0 answers)

- Authwit: **e2e + playground UI panel** (manual QA surface).
- cancelJob ownership: **silent no-op** on profile mismatch (idempotent contract preserved; deliberate behavior change to a previously-pinned behavior — pins updated, not violated).
- Done bar: **CI green incl. the new lifecycle e2e + one manual authwit pass by the user**. No RC ceremony.
- CI placement: new e2e joins the **regular 5-way shards**.

## The consumer-shape decision (primary vs competing outline)

### Outline A (primary): custom `AuthwitGate` fixture contract

A minimal Noir contract with one entrypoint, `pull_public(from, token, amount, nonce)`, that internally calls `Token.transfer_in_public(from, self, amount, nonce)` — forcing the token to check the canonical AuthRegistry for `from`'s authorization of AuthwitGate as caller. This models the REAL dApp shape (a contract consumer, DEX-style), which is what wallet users actually grant authwits to.

- Lives in a new `packages/fixture-contracts/authwit_gate/` (single-responsibility; bridge-aztec stays production-only), compiled via the bridge-aztec `compile.sh` pattern (rc.2 toolchain, committed transpiled `target/*.json`).
- Deployed by `deployContractsAndProvide` (`global-setup.ts:491`) next to the test token; address added to `AztecTestConfig`.

### Outline B (competing, cheapest-first): two-account canonical-token path

No new contract: account A grants a public authwit naming account B as caller for `transfer_in_public(A → B)`; B sends the transfer; the token checks the registry. Zero Noir, zero new package.

- Rejected as primary (see ledger D1): the consumer is an ACCOUNT, not a contract — it does not model the dApp-grants flow users actually hit, the wallet e2e has thin multi-account support (only `fixtures/helpers.ts` touches account creation), and driving a SECOND wallet account through the popup doubles e2e choreography. Kept as documented fallback if the rc.2 compile pipeline proves brittle in CI (bail-out path for Phase 1).

## Phases

### Phase 0 — Baselines + housekeeping (0.25d)
- Add the missing `incoming-trust-state-machine-refactor` entry to `implementations-plan/index.md` (index discipline; shipped as PR #75).
- Characterization: pin CURRENT `cancelJob` accepts-any-id behavior in `execution-lane.test.ts` as `(BUG PIN)` marked for deliberate change in Phase 4 (so the change is visible as a pin REPLACEMENT, not a silent edit).
- **Validation gate**: `bun run lint` exit 0; `bunx vitest run src/wallet/services/execution/execution-lane.test.ts` green (layers: lint · unit).

### Phase 1 — `AuthwitGate` fixture contract (0.5-1d)
- New `packages/fixture-contracts/` package: `authwit_gate/` Nargo project (aztec-nr pinned to the same v4.2.0-aztecnr-rc.2 tag bridge-aztec uses), `pull_public` entrypoint per Outline A; `compile.sh` adapted from `packages/bridge-aztec/scripts/compile.sh`; committed transpiled artifact.
- Unit test: artifact loads via `loadContractArtifact` (the transpile-check aztec.js performs) + selector/function-shape pins.
- **Validation gate**: `compile.sh` exits 0 locally; `bun run lint` + new artifact-load unit test green (layers: lint · unit). BAIL-OUT: if the rc.2 toolchain cannot produce a CI-loadable artifact in ≤5 attempts, switch to Outline B (documented, user informed — not silent).

### Phase 2 — Deploy + playground consume panel (0.5d)
- `global-setup.ts` deploys AuthwitGate; `AztecTestConfig` + lockfile gain `authwitGateAddress`.
- Playground `sections/authwit.ts` extended: "consume (pull_public)" button — sends a dApp tx calling `AuthwitGate.pull_public(from, token, amount, nonce)` via the normal wallet sendTx flow; result row carries ok/error (`pg-result` testid convention). The wallet's builder auto-injects the `set_authorized` grant on first use (`tx-request-builder.ts:252` hook) and `trackAuthwit` records it — making the grant visible in settings for the revoke step.
- **Validation gate**: `bun run e2e:agent tests/e2e/network/<smoke-of-consume>.test.ts` — a minimal consume-once test green; lint + unit suites green (layers: lint · unit · e2e-network).

### Phase 3 — Lifecycle e2e (0.5-1d)
- New `tests/e2e/network/authwit-lifecycle.test.ts` (regular shard pool): grant-on-first-consume → consume OK → settings reveal the tracked authwit → **revoke via `RevokeAuthwitsPopup` testids** → consume FAILS → **registry disable via `ChangeAuthwitsRegistryPopup` testids** → consume fails → re-enable → consume OK again. Selectors: data-testid only (house rule); add missing testids to the two popups BEFORE writing the test.
- **Validation gate**: `bun run e2e:agent tests/e2e/network/authwit-lifecycle.test.ts` green ×2 consecutive locally; full `bun run e2e:agent` green (layers: e2e-network full).

### Phase 4 — Execution follow-ups batch (0.5d)
- **cancelJob ownership**: `ExecutionLane.cancelJob` loads the record (`operationJournal.getOperation(id)` — `service.ts:364`), and if `record.profileId !== activeProfile.id`, drops the cancel silently (same observable behavior as unknown id). New lane dep: `getActiveProfile` (already injected). Replace the Phase-0 bug pin with the new ownership pins (match + mismatch + record-absent).
- **`dapp_execute` start-path unification**: move `beginDappExecuteJournal` from the facade into `ExecutionLane` (it already receives `createFreshRecord` — invert: the lane owns the factory; the facade delegate and the executor `beginJournal` wiring both point at the lane). Zero behavior change; existing claim-helper + executor tests stay green untouched.
- **`E2E_REQUIRE_SETUP` node-health**: in `global-setup.ts`, when `E2E_REQUIRE_SETUP=1` and the local node fails health (`waitForLocalNode`, `fixtures/aztec.ts:66`), throw loudly instead of letting suites soft-skip (observed: bb SIGILL → node unhealthy → `5 skipped`, exit 0).
- **Validation gate**: `bun run lint` + `bun run test` exit 0; lane unit suite green incl. new ownership pins; a deliberate node-kill dry-run shows the loud failure (layers: lint · unit; manual probe for the setup gate).

### Phase 5 — Arc close (0.5d)
- `/code-review max --fix` (separate commit) → codex post-impl audit (net diff + code-review summary + this plan + adversarial ask) → fix loop → docs (playground README note, fixture-contracts README) → single PR to dev → **user's manual authwit pass on the playground panel** gates merge.
- **Validation gate**: CI green on the PR (Quality required; Network e2e incl. the new file in shards); codex post-impl verdict with high/critical addressed.

## Security & Adversarial Considerations

- **Threat model**: the fixture contract is TEST-ONLY but ships in-repo; it must never be deployed outside sandbox flows (no production wiring; playground consume panel only acts on user-confirmed wallet popups). An attacker-controlled dApp gains nothing new: the consume path exercises EXISTING wallet flows (sendTx + registry writes) behind the same approval popups.
- **cancelJob authz**: silent no-op chosen over explicit error specifically so probing for foreign job ids leaks nothing (existence non-disclosure); the check compares against the ACTIVE profile server-side (SW), not caller-supplied data.
- **Registry semantics**: revoke and registry-disable are on-chain writes via the user's own account — fee-paying, popup-confirmed; the e2e asserts the FAILURE of consumption after revoke (negative test), which is the security property that matters.
- **Supply chain**: no new npm deps; Noir toolchain is the already-pinned local rc.2 install; committed artifacts are reviewed like code (transpiled JSON diffs are large — reviewer checks the source `.nr` + compile.sh reproducibility instead).
- **Crypto**: no custom crypto; authwit hashing stays in aztec.js (`computeAuthWitMessageHash`) and the account contract.

## Assumptions

### Facts (verified)
- Playground grants but never consumes: `packages/playground/src/sections/authwit.ts` (createAuthWit callIntent/innerHash only, 92 lines).
- Revoke/toggle UI exists: `RevokeAuthwitsPopup.vue`, `ChangeAuthwitsRegistryPopup.vue`, `settings/advanced/account-state/authwits/index.vue`.
- `revokeAuthwits` sends `set_authorized` via `executeSendTransaction` (`auth-registry/service.ts:93-120`); `setRegistryEnabled` at `:149`.
- Builder injects registry writes during sendTx builds: `tx-request-builder.ts:252` region (`getAuthRegistryAddress`/`getSetAuthorizedFn`); `trackAuthwit` records grants (`auth-registry/service.ts:73`).
- Noir compile precedent: `packages/bridge-aztec/scripts/compile.sh` (rc.2 toolchain, transpile via `aztec compile`, committed `target/*.json`).
- e2e deploy hook: `deployContractsAndProvide` (`global-setup.ts:491`) with lockfile reuse; `OperationRecord.profileId` exists (`operation-journal/spec.ts:65`); `getOperation` exists (`operation-journal/service.ts:364`).
- Soft-skip gap reproduced: node startup failure under `E2E_REQUIRE_SETUP=1` yields `skipped`, exit 0 (PR #83 comment, docker run evidence).

### Inferences (attack targets)
- The builder's `set_authorized` injection fires for a CONTRACT consumer on the `pull_public` path exactly as it does for existing flows, and `trackAuthwit` captures it (the hook was verified to exist; the precise trigger conditions on this path are deduced, not yet traced end-to-end).
- The rc.2 `aztec compile` toolchain produces artifacts loadable by the wallet's aztec.js 4.2.0 at e2e runtime (true for bridge-aztec's contracts; assumed transferable).
- `Token.transfer_in_public` (the canonical test token) checks the AuthRegistry when `from != msg_sender` — standard aztec-nr token behavior at this pin.
- Revoking the tracked authwit invalidates EXACTLY the consume path (message-hash equality between the grant the builder injected and the hash the settings revoke targets).

### Asks
- None open — Phase 0 answers resolved scope, authz semantics, done bar, and CI placement. (Outline B remains a pre-authorized bail-out for Phase 1, not an ask.)

| D1 | Outline A (contract consumer) over Outline B (two-account) | main draft | B models account-callers, not the dApp-contract grants users actually approve; thin e2e multi-account support; B kept as Phase-1 bail-out. AUDIT QUESTION: is B actually sufficient for the lifecycle properties? |
| D2 | cancelJob: silent no-op over explicit error | user (Phase 0) | Error shape leaks job-id existence + adds RPC surface. |

    30	function safe<T>(method: string, fn: () => Promise<T>): () => Promise<void> {
    31		return async () => {
    32			const wallet = getWallet()
    33			if (!wallet) {
    34				setState({ lastError: "Not connected — call connect() first" })

    36			}
    37			try {
    38				await logCall(method, fn)
    39			} catch (err) {
    40				setState({ lastError: err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err) })
    41			}
    42		}
    43	}

    48			safe("createAuthWit", async () => {

    51				if (!s.selectedAccount) throw new Error("No selected account")
    52				const consumer = getInput("consumer") || getInput("tokenAddress")
    53				if (!consumer) throw new Error("consumer or tokenAddress required")
    54				const fromAddr = AztecAddress.fromString(s.selectedAccount)
    55				const consumerAddr = AztecAddress.fromString(consumer)
    56				const intent = {
    57					caller: consumerAddr,
    58					call: FunctionCall.from({
    59						name: "transfer_public_to_public",
    60						to: consumerAddr,
    61						selector: await FunctionSelector.fromSignature("transfer_public_to_public((Field),(Field),Field,Field)"),
    62						type: FunctionType.PUBLIC,
    63						hideMsgSender: false,
    64						isStatic: false,
    65						args: [],
    66						returnTypes: [],
    67					}),
    68				}
    69				// biome-ignore lint/suspicious/noExplicitAny: CallIntent shape varies by aztec.js version
    70				return wallet.createAuthWit(fromAddr, intent as any)
    71			}),
    72		)
    73	
    74		root.querySelector<HTMLButtonElement>('[data-testid="pg-btn-createAuthWit-innerHash"]')?.addEventListener(
    75			"click",
    76			safe("createAuthWit", async () => {

ARCHITECTURE.md:94:- **Operation journal model** (Phase 2 + Phase 2.5). Every long-running operation creates a record with a 7-stage FSM (`pending → simulating → proving → submitting → succeeded/failed/cancelled`, plus a `simulating → succeeded` no-prove shortcut for non-tx kinds). Three kinds today: `transfer`, `dapp_execute` (full FSM + on-chain `txHash`), `token_import` (no-prove shortcut, no `txHash`). The kind ↔ `txHash` invariant is enforced at `transitionOperation`. Sibling `JournalReaper` marks stuck non-terminal records as failed; `JournalGC` caps terminal records at 50 per `(profileId, accountAddress)` on a 60-min alarm. Activity feed renders one card per in-flight journal op (newest on top, older below); token-import surface is a sibling `TokenImportRow` in the tokens view. The substrate is intentionally extensible — adding a new kind requires adding the enum variant + the `kind ↔ txHash` branch + a renderer; the FSM table stays unchanged.
ARCHITECTURE.md:147:A `DappSession` is per-`(origin, chainId, profileId)`. When the dApp's profile or chain changes, the session is revoked and re-approval is required. Auto-approve runs when an active session matches the discovery request.
ARCHITECTURE.md:192:Fee-method selection persists per `(profileId, networkId, accountAddress)`. A storage migration drops the saved selection when the FPC schema changes so a dangling FPC id from a pre-v4 record cannot resolve to a stale handler.

If a future feature ever adds `externally_connectable: { matches: ["..."] }` (e.g. for a dev playground), any external page in the allowed list could send forged PXE requests with arbitrary `from`/`to` fields, hitting privileged operations like `registerAccount` (which writes derived secret keys into PXE storage at `pxe/${profileId}/${chainId}/`).
audit/security/2026-06-08-ultra-e6759a/raw/C8-claude-1.md:215:The `proveTx` timeout is 30 minutes; the comment says this is because BB.wasm proving is uninterruptible and Phase 2 `cancelJob` is the user-facing cancel path (lossy: SW marks cancelled, offscreen keeps running). The lock semantics are correct, but the long timeout chained with the per-chain write lock means **a runaway/stuck proveTx blocks all other writes on that chain for up to 30 minutes**. Other chains are unaffected.

packages/bridge-aztec/token_bridge/target/token_bridge_contract-TokenBridge.json:85:      "source": "//! The `self` contract value for public execution contexts.\n\nuse crate::{\n    context::{calls::{PublicCall, PublicStaticCall}, PublicContext},\n    event::{event_emission::emit_event_in_public, event_interface::EventInterface},\n};\nuse crate::protocol::{address::AztecAddress, traits::{Deserialize, Serialize}};\n\n/// Core interface for interacting with aztec-nr contract features in public execution contexts.\n///\n/// This struct is automatically injected into every [`external`](crate::macros::functions::external) and\n/// [`internal`](crate::macros::functions::internal) contract function marked with `\"public\"` by the Aztec macro\n/// system and is accessible through the `self` variable.\n///\n/// ## Type Parameters\n///\n/// - `Storage`: The contract's storage struct (defined with [`storage`](crate::macros::storage::storage), or `()` if\n/// the contract has no storage\n/// - `CallSelf`: Macro-generated type for calling contract's own non-view functions\n/// - `CallSelfStatic`: Macro-generated type for calling contract's own view functions\n/// - `CallInternal`: Macro-generated type for calling internal functions\npub struct ContractSelfPublic<Storage, CallSelf, CallSelfStatic, CallInternal> {\n    /// The address of this contract\n    pub address: AztecAddress,\n\n    /// The contract's storage instance, representing the struct to which the\n    /// [`storage`](crate::macros::storage::storage) macro was applied in your contract. If the contract has no\n    /// storage, the type of this will be `()`.\n    ///\n    /// This storage instance is specialized for the current execution context (public) and\n    /// provides access to the contract's state variables.\n    ///\n    /// ## Developer Note\n    ///\n    /// If you've arrived here while trying to access your contract's storage while the `Storage` generic type is set\n    /// to unit type `()`, it means you haven't yet defined a Storage struct using the\n    /// [`storage`](crate::macros::storage::storage) macro in your contract. For guidance on setting this up, please\n    /// refer to our docs: https://docs.aztec.network/developers/docs/guides/smart_contracts/storage\n    pub storage: Storage,\n\n    /// The public execution context.\n    pub context: PublicContext,\n\n    /// Provides type-safe methods for calling this contract's own non-view functions.\n    ///\n    /// Example API:\n    /// ```noir\n    /// self.call_self.some_public_function(args)\n    /// ```\n    pub call_self: CallSelf,\n\n    /// Provides type-safe methods for calling this contract's own view functions.\n    ///\n    /// Example API:\n    /// ```noir\n    /// self.call_self_static.some_view_function(args)\n    /// ```\n    pub call_self_static: CallSelfStatic,\n\n    /// Provides type-safe methods for calling internal functions.\n    ///\n    /// Example API:\n    /// ```noir\n    /// self.internal.some_internal_function(args)\n    /// ```\n    pub internal: CallInternal,\n}\n\nimpl<Storage, CallSelf, CallSelfStatic, CallInternal> ContractSelfPublic<Storage, CallSelf, CallSelfStatic, CallInternal> {\n    /// Creates a new `ContractSelfPublic` instance for a public function.\n    ///\n    /// This constructor is called automatically by the macro system and should not be called directly.\n    pub fn new(\n        context: PublicContext,\n        storage: Storage,\n        call_self: CallSelf,\n        call_self_static: CallSelfStatic,\n        internal: CallInternal,\n    ) -> Self {\n        Self { context, storage, address: context.this_address(), call_self, call_self_static, internal }\n    }\n\n    /// The address of the contract address that made this function call.\n    ///\n    /// This is similar to Solidity's `msg.sender` value.\n    ///\n    /// ## Incognito Calls\n    ///\n    /// Contracts can call public functions from private ones hiding their identity (see\n    ///\n    /// [`ContractSelfPrivate::enqueue_incognito`](crate::contract_self::ContractSelfPrivate::enqueue_incognito)).\n    /// This function reverts when executed in such a context.\n    ///\n    /// If you need to handle these cases, use [`PublicContext::maybe_msg_sender`].\n    pub fn msg_sender(self: Self) -> AztecAddress {\n        self.context.maybe_msg_sender().unwrap()\n    }\n\n    /// Emits an event publicly.\n    ///\n    /// Public events are emitted as plaintext and are therefore visible to everyone. This is is the same as Solidity\n    /// events on EVM chains.\n    ///\n    /// Unlike private events, they don't require delivery of an event message.\n    ///\n    /// # Example\n    /// ```noir\n    /// #[event]\n    /// struct Update { value: Field }\n    ///\n    /// #[external(\"public\")]\n    /// fn publish_update(value: Field) {\n    ///     self.emit(Update { value });\n    /// }\n    /// ```\n    ///\n    /// # Cost\n    ///\n    /// Public event emission is achieved by emitting public transaction logs. A total of `N+1` fields are emitted,\n    /// where `N` is the serialization length of the event.\n    pub fn emit<Event>(&mut self, event: Event)\n    where\n        Event: EventInterface + Serialize,\n    {\n        emit_event_in_public(self.context, event);\n    }\n\n    /// Makes a public contract call.\n    ///\n    /// Will revert if the called function reverts or runs out of gas.\n    ///\n    /// # Arguments\n    /// * `call` - The object representing the public function to invoke.\n    ///\n    /// # Returns\n    /// * `T` - Whatever data the called function has returned.\n    ///\n    /// # Example\n    /// ```noir\n    /// self.call(Token::at(address).transfer_in_public(recipient, amount));\n    /// ```\n    ///\n    pub unconstrained fn call<let M: u32, let N: u32, T>(self, call: PublicCall<M, N, T>) -> T\n    where\n        T: Deserialize,\n    {\n        call.call(self.context)\n    }\n\n    /// Makes a public read-only contract call.\n    ///\n    /// This is similar to Solidity's `staticcall`. The called function cannot modify state or emit events. Any nested\n    /// calls are constrained to also be static calls.\n    ///\n    /// Will revert if the called function reverts or runs out of gas.\n    ///\n    /// # Arguments\n    /// * `call` - The object representing the read-only public function to invoke.\n    ///\n    /// # Returns\n    /// * `T` - Whatever data the called function has returned.\n    ///\n    /// # Example\n    /// ```noir\n    /// self.view(Token::at(address).balance_of_public(recipient));\n    /// ```\n    ///\n    pub unconstrained fn view<let M: u32, let N: u32, T>(self, call: PublicStaticCall<M, N, T>) -> T\n    where\n        T: Deserialize,\n    {\n        call.view(self.context)\n    }\n}\n"

wallets-architecture-research/nulo-phase-2.html:175:  Phase 2's premise: <strong>stop pretending the SW will stay alive</strong>. Treat any in-flight job that survives the worker as a <em>feature</em>, not a corner case. Submit jobs that return immediately with a <code>jobId</code>. Persist state aggressively. Subscribe to job state from the popup, not via blocking calls. Wire <code>AbortController</code> through prove and sim. Partition PXE concurrency per <code>(profileId, chainId)</code> so different chains don't block each other. Use <code>chrome.alarms</code> to resume work on cold boot. Use <code>LazyListener</code> so events that fire during initialization don't get lost.

audit/security/2026-06-08-ultra-e6759a/raw/C6-claude-1.md:388:- Exploitability: AV:Local / AC:Medium / PR:None / UI:Required. Time window: between profile switch and `closeWindow` settling, the user could click Confirm and observe weird UX. The actual transaction does NOT execute against the wrong profile (the SW's `executeAndResolve` at `dapp-interaction/service.ts:140-147` re-validates `payload.session.profileId === active?.id`), so this is a UX-bug-leaning-toward-confusion, not a privilege-escalation. But it weakens the trust posture of the approval surface.
audit/security/2026-06-08-ultra-e6759a/raw/C6-claude-1.md:417:**Title**: `capabilities/index.vue:171-223` `approve()` is invoked on a Button click. The early-return checks `needsAccountSelection.value && selectedAccounts.value.length === 0` (`:184`). Then it spreads `selectedAccounts.value.map(...)` into `resultSelectedAccounts` at `:203` and iterates at `:205-208` for the alias map. Between the `:184` check and the `:203` snapshot, there is NO sync barrier — but Vue's microtask scheduling means there's no JS yield, so this is safe. However, the AccountSelectRow's `:disabled="isLoading || processingError?.type === 'error'"` (`:304`) gates user clicks during the `await interactionService.resolveInteraction(...)` await at `:211`. Critically, `isLoading.value = true` is set at `:189` BEFORE the snapshot at `:203` — so the disabled gate IS active. UI race is contained. **HOWEVER**: `availableAccounts` (`:113`) is set from `payload.params.availableAccounts` — a dApp-supplied list per the wire (`CapabilityParams.availableAccounts`). A malicious dApp providing inflated `availableAccounts` is gated by the dispatcher at `dispatcher.ts:566-575` which OVERWRITES `availableAccounts` from `accountService.getAccounts(profileId, chainId)` — so the dApp's wire value is replaced with the wallet's own list before the popup sees it. Confirmed by reading `dispatcher.ts:566-575`. So the popup CAN trust `availableAccounts`. Status of this finding: **NULL** — popup-side selection accounting is correct; closing as no-finding for documentation.

The service's downstream code does `parseCaipAccount` and other parsing, but doesn't structurally validate `profileId`, `networkId`, `contract`, `accountAddress`. A malformed `networkId` cannot collide with a real one (key shape uses `@`), but `contract` is part of the `|`-delimited trust key — a contract containing `|` would collide with a different `(profileId, networkId, contract)` triple. See C7-5.

audit/security/2026-06-08-ultra-e6759a/findings/verified.md:28:**Strengthened fix**: Pass `sender.frameId` + `sender.url` into the upstream handler (this likely needs a wallet-sdk patch — the upstream API already accepts `sender`, but it picks `.tab?.url`). Additionally, key sessions by `(origin, frameId, chainId, profileId)` instead of `(origin, chainId, profileId)`, and reject DISCOVERY_REQUEST messages whose `sender.frameId !== 0` unless subframe discovery is an explicit product requirement. Pattern: see how `chrome.tabs.sendMessage` accepts `{ frameId }` — mirror that in the relay layer. Until the wallet-sdk patch lands, a Nulo-side defense is to inspect the raw `sender` inside the `addContentListener` wrapper at `background.ts:121-135` and refuse non-top frames before calling `listener(message, sender)`.
audit/security/2026-06-08-ultra-e6759a/findings/verified.md:108:**Strengthened fix**: In `initWalletSdkHandler`, subscribe to `dappSessionService.onDappSessionDeleted` and call `handler.terminateSession(session.sessionId)` for any matching active session. The wallet-sdk's `ActiveSession` carries `origin` + `chainInfo`, so the matching predicate is `(s) => s.origin === deletedSession.origin && chainInfoToChainId(s) === deletedSession.chainId && s.profileId === deletedSession.profileId` (mirrors the `tryGetDappSessionByOriginAndChain` lookup). Also wire the same teardown on `deleteExpired` / `isExpired`. wallets-architecture-research/nulo/self-analysis.md:290:- **Where does the unlocked secret live during a sendTx flow?** `ProfileService.getProfileSecret(profileId)` (called by `AccountService.deriveAccountSecret`) returns the `Fr` from `SessionManager.getSecret`. Account secret is then `poseidon2Hash([master, chainId, type, index])`. The master `Fr` is held the entire SW lifetime. wallets-architecture-research/README.md:19:**The one architectural area where Nulo is materially behind every other wallet is long-running operations.** Both the Claude self-analysis and the Codex critical review converge on the same diagnosis: the popup-to-SW execution path defaults to a 60-second `ServiceClient` timeout, healthy proofs can routinely outrun that, "timeout" is not "cancellation" so the SW keeps proving while the popup shows failure, fee-estimation cancellation only bumps a stale counter (no `AbortController` in the prove path — `grep` returns 0 hits), PXE concurrency is globally serialized behind one `ReadWriteGuard` instead of per-(profileId, chainId), in-flight prove state is not persisted, and there is no `chrome.alarms` wake-up to keep the wallet ready for incoming dApp messages between popup sessions. Rabby and MetaMask both ship better long-running-job patterns (Rabby's resumable history sync, MetaMask's `unlockPromise` semantics, `LazyListener` boot-time event buffering, deferred-promise port gating). For an Aztec wallet whose tx latency is *measured in seconds-to-minutes*, this is the section to fix first.

packages/bridge-aztec/token_minter_proxy/target/token_minter_proxy-TokenMinterProxy.json:81:      "source": "//! The `self` contract value for public execution contexts.\n\nuse crate::{\n    context::{calls::{PublicCall, PublicStaticCall}, PublicContext},\n    event::{event_emission::emit_event_in_public, event_interface::EventInterface},\n};\nuse crate::protocol::{address::AztecAddress, traits::{Deserialize, Serialize}};\n\n/// Core interface for interacting with aztec-nr contract features in public execution contexts.\n///\n/// This struct is automatically injected into every [`external`](crate::macros::functions::external) and\n/// [`internal`](crate::macros::functions::internal) contract function marked with `\"public\"` by the Aztec macro\n/// system and is accessible through the `self` variable.\n///\n/// ## Type Parameters\n///\n/// - `Storage`: The contract's storage struct (defined with [`storage`](crate::macros::storage::storage), or `()` if\n/// the contract has no storage\n/// - `CallSelf`: Macro-generated type for calling contract's own non-view functions\n/// - `CallSelfStatic`: Macro-generated type for calling contract's own view functions\n/// - `CallInternal`: Macro-generated type for calling internal functions\npub struct ContractSelfPublic<Storage, CallSelf, CallSelfStatic, CallInternal> {\n    /// The address of this contract\n    pub address: AztecAddress,\n\n    /// The contract's storage instance, representing the struct to which the\n    /// [`storage`](crate::macros::storage::storage) macro was applied in your contract. If the contract has no\n    /// storage, the type of this will be `()`.\n    ///\n    /// This storage instance is specialized for the current execution context (public) and\n    /// provides access to the contract's state variables.\n    ///\n    /// ## Developer Note\n    ///\n    /// If you've arrived here while trying to access your contract's storage while the `Storage` generic type is set\n    /// to unit type `()`, it means you haven't yet defined a Storage struct using the\n    /// [`storage`](crate::macros::storage::storage) macro in your contract. For guidance on setting this up, please\n    /// refer to our docs: https://docs.aztec.network/developers/docs/guides/smart_contracts/storage\n    pub storage: Storage,\n\n    /// The public execution context.\n    pub context: PublicContext,\n\n    /// Provides type-safe methods for calling this contract's own non-view functions.\n    ///\n    /// Example API:\n    /// ```noir\n    /// self.call_self.some_public_function(args)\n    /// ```\n    pub call_self: CallSelf,\n\n    /// Provides type-safe methods for calling this contract's own view functions.\n    ///\n    /// Example API:\n    /// ```noir\n    /// self.call_self_static.some_view_function(args)\n    /// ```\n    pub call_self_static: CallSelfStatic,\n\n    /// Provides type-safe methods for calling internal functions.\n    ///\n    /// Example API:\n    /// ```noir\n    /// self.internal.some_internal_function(args)\n    /// ```\n    pub internal: CallInternal,\n}\n\nimpl<Storage, CallSelf, CallSelfStatic, CallInternal> ContractSelfPublic<Storage, CallSelf, CallSelfStatic, CallInternal> {\n    /// Creates a new `ContractSelfPublic` instance for a public function.\n    ///\n    /// This constructor is called automatically by the macro system and should not be called directly.\n    pub fn new(\n        context: PublicContext,\n        storage: Storage,\n        call_self: CallSelf,\n        call_self_static: CallSelfStatic,\n        internal: CallInternal,\n    ) -> Self {\n        Self { context, storage, address: context.this_address(), call_self, call_self_static, internal }\n    }\n\n    /// The address of the contract address that made this function call.\n    ///\n    /// This is similar to Solidity's `msg.sender` value.\n    ///\n    /// ## Incognito Calls\n    ///\n    /// Contracts can call public functions from private ones hiding their identity (see\n    ///\n    /// [`ContractSelfPrivate::enqueue_incognito`](crate::contract_self::ContractSelfPrivate::enqueue_incognito)).\n    /// This function reverts when executed in such a context.\n    ///\n    /// If you need to handle these cases, use [`PublicContext::maybe_msg_sender`].\n    pub fn msg_sender(self: Self) -> AztecAddress {\n        self.context.maybe_msg_sender().unwrap()\n    }\n\n    /// Emits an event publicly.\n    ///\n    /// Public events are emitted as plaintext and are therefore visible to everyone. This is is the same as Solidity\n    /// events on EVM chains.\n    ///\n    /// Unlike private events, they don't require delivery of an event message.\n    ///\n    /// # Example\n    /// ```noir\n    /// #[event]\n    /// struct Update { value: Field }\n    ///\n    /// #[external(\"public\")]\n    /// fn publish_update(value: Field) {\n    ///     self.emit(Update { value });\n    /// }\n    /// ```\n    ///\n    /// # Cost\n    ///\n    /// Public event emission is achieved by emitting public transaction logs. A total of `N+1` fields are emitted,\n    /// where `N` is the serialization length of the event.\n    pub fn emit<Event>(&mut self, event: Event)\n    where\n        Event: EventInterface + Serialize,\n    {\n        emit_event_in_public(self.context, event);\n    }\n\n    /// Makes a public contract call.\n    ///\n    /// Will revert if the called function reverts or runs out of gas.\n    ///\n    /// # Arguments\n    /// * `call` - The object representing the public function to invoke.\n    ///\n    /// # Returns\n    /// * `T` - Whatever data the called function has returned.\n    ///\n    /// # Example\n    /// ```noir\n    /// self.call(Token::at(address).transfer_in_public(recipient, amount));\n    /// ```\n    ///\n    pub unconstrained fn call<let M: u32, let N: u32, T>(self, call: PublicCall<M, N, T>) -> T\n    where\n        T: Deserialize,\n    {\n        call.call(self.context)\n    }\n\n    /// Makes a public read-only contract call.\n    ///\n    /// This is similar to Solidity's `staticcall`. The called function cannot modify state or emit events. Any nested\n    /// calls are constrained to also be static calls.\n    ///\n    /// Will revert if the called function reverts or runs out of gas.\n    ///\n    /// # Arguments\n    /// * `call` - The object representing the read-only public function to invoke.\n    ///\n    /// # Returns\n    /// * `T` - Whatever data the called function has returned.\n    ///\n    /// # Example\n    /// ```noir\n    /// self.view(Token::at(address).balance_of_public(recipient));\n    /// ```\n    ///\n    pub unconstrained fn view<let M: u32, let N: u32, T>(self, call: PublicStaticCall<M, N, T>) -> T\n    where\n        T: Deserialize,\n    {\n        call.view(self.context)\n    }\n}\n"

If it is acquired before `planner.processAztecJsPayload`, authwit discovery, claim, and build, and held through submit for both standard and `NO_FROM`, only one approved tx per `(profileId, chainId)` can touch PXE execution state at a time ([service.ts](/Users/alejoamiras/Projects/nulo/nulo-1/packages/extension/src/wallet/services/execution/service.ts:1695), [service.ts](/Users/alejoamiras/Projects/nulo/nulo-1/packages/extension/src/wallet/services/execution/service.ts:1831)). Popup concurrency by itself is fine; execution concurrency is the risky part.
implementations-plan/dapp-interaction-lock-fix-v3/audit-codex.md:21:5. `#5` `P1` — Cancel-while-mutex-waiting can be sound, but not with the current “existing cancel infrastructure” alone. Today `cancelJob` flips the journal to `cancelled` and then aborts a controller from `activeControllers` ([execution/service.ts](/Users/alejoamiras/Projects/nulo/nulo-1/packages/extension/src/wallet/services/execution/service.ts:799)). Those controllers are only registered after claim/create ([claim-helper.ts](/Users/alejoamiras/Projects/nulo/nulo-1/packages/extension/src/wallet/services/execution/claim-helper.ts:129)). If claim moves after mutex acquire, a queued waiter has no controller yet, so `mutex.acquire(signal)` will not wake unless you add a waiter-abort registry before enqueueing. With that added, the 4001 chain is sound: sentinel -> cancelled result -> `JobCancelledError` -> wallet-sdk 4001 ([rpc-cancel.ts](/Users/alejoamiras/Projects/nulo/nulo-1/packages/extension/src/wallet/services/execution/rpc-cancel.ts:47), [dispatcher.ts](/Users/alejoamiras/Projects/nulo/nulo-1/packages/wallet-bridge/src/dispatcher.ts:117), [error-envelope.ts](/Users/alejoamiras/Projects/nulo/nulo-1/packages/extension/src/wallet/services/wallet-sdk/error-envelope.ts:22)). I do not see an inherent deadlock if acquire stays `exec-mutex -> journal` and cancel stays `journal -> waiter-abort`.
implementations-plan/dapp-interaction-lock-fix-v3/audit-codex-final.md:6:If the mutex is acquired before [executeAztecSendTx](/Users/alejoamiras/Projects/nulo/nulo-1/packages/extension/src/wallet/services/execution/service.ts:1695) and [executeNoFromSendTx](/Users/alejoamiras/Projects/nulo/nulo-1/packages/extension/src/wallet/services/execution/service.ts:1831), and released only after submit, it closes both holes. Everything before that boundary is non-PXE/journal-only or pure parsing: [processAztecJsPayload](/Users/alejoamiras/Projects/nulo/nulo-1/packages/extension/src/wallet/services/execution/operation-planner.ts:152), queued-record creation [queued-journal.ts](/Users/alejoamiras/Projects/nulo/nulo-1/packages/extension/src/wallet/services/wallet-sdk/queued-journal.ts:144), silent fast-forward [dapp-interaction/service.ts](/Users/alejoamiras/Projects/nulo/nulo-1/packages/extension/src/wallet/services/dapp-interaction/service.ts:295). The first PXE-touching work on the standard path is authwit discovery/build/simulate [execution/service.ts](/Users/alejoamiras/Projects/nulo/nulo-1/packages/extension/src/wallet/services/execution/service.ts:1754), [authwit-discoverer.ts](/Users/alejoamiras/Projects/nulo/nulo-1/packages/extension/src/wallet/services/execution/authwit-discoverer.ts:71); on NO_FROM it is build/register/simulate [execution/service.ts](/Users/alejoamiras/Projects/nulo/nulo-1/packages/extension/src/wallet/services/execution/service.ts:1867), [tx-request-builder.ts](/Users/alejoamiras/Projects/nulo/nulo-1/packages/extension/src/wallet/services/execution/tx-request-builder.ts:395). implementations-plan/dapp-interaction-lock-fix-v3/plan.md:90:Both audits, P1. Today `cancelJob` flips journal → cancelled, then aborts a controller from `activeControllers` — but those controllers are registered only **after** claim (`claim-helper.ts:129/141`). With claim now after acquire, a waiting T2 has **no controller** → cancel can't wake `mutex.acquire(signal)` → delayed cancel (T2's promise doesn't reject until T1 finishes).
implementations-plan/dapp-interaction-lock-fix-v3/plan.md:94:**Edge (final codex pass):** the claim-helper retains a `record-not-found → createFreshRecord()` fallback (`claim-helper.ts:80`). If that path fires, the pre-registered controller keyed by `queuedJournalId` is orphaned (the fresh record has a different id). Migrate the controller entry to the fresh id, or delete it, on that branch — else the key leaks and the fresh id has no waiter controller. Edge cleanup, not a broader refactor. (`queuedJournalId` === the claimed record id on the normal path, so `cancelJob(id)` finds the same controller — confirmed.)

implementations-plan/capabilities-popup-quality/audit-opus.md:13:- **`contracts.canRegister` framing — caveat.** Plan keeps "Register contracts" unchanged labeled silent. But `register_contract` (lower-case wire kind, see `service.ts:381`) returns `AccessLevel.PxeState`. The default session `confirmationLevel` per the codebase is `AppState` ≥ `PxeState`, so silent. **However:** `service.ts:347-349` short-circuits with `return true` when the active profile id doesn't match the session's `profileId`. If the user switches profiles, *every* register call triggers a popup. Plan doesn't mention this nuance — minor. Acceptable to leave as "silent" since the wrong-profile case is degenerate.
implementations-plan/dapp-interaction-lock-fix-v3/lessons/phase-0.md:15:1. **Phase 2 (ExecutionMutex)** — pure abortable FIFO mutex + wire into both send paths; claim-after-acquire; pre-acquire controller; key (profileId, chainId). Inert while the baton still serializes at handler-completion (uncontended acquire) → all existing tests stay green. Riskiest piece → codex-audit before moving on.
implementations-plan/dapp-interaction-lock-fix-v3/lessons/phase-0.md:26:- **2b** (commit): wired into both send paths. `resolveExecutionMutexKey(networkId)` → `(profileId, chainId)` matching the PXE chainGuard. `acquire` before claim + any PXE work; `releaseSlot()` in the existing `finally`; claim moved after acquire (so a future waiter stays `queued`). Uncontended while the baton still serializes at handler-completion → behavior-neutral. Verified: typecheck ✓, 163 execution tests ✓, audit:vue ✓.
implementations-plan/dapp-interaction-lock-fix-v3/lessons/phase-0.md:29:Key granularity decision: keyed `(profileId, chainId)` NOT `networkId`. If a profile ever holds two network rows for one chainId, keying by networkId would under-serialize vs the chainGuard (which keys by profileId+chainId). Paying one extra `getNetwork` lookup before acquire (metadata-only, non-PXE) buys exact-match correctness.
implementations-plan/dapp-interaction-lock-fix-v3/lessons/phase-0.md:35:- **Pre-acquire controller (cancel-during-wait):** `acquireExecutionSlot(networkId, queuedJournalId)` registers an AbortController under `queuedJournalId` BEFORE `executionMutex.acquire(key, signal)`. Abort → `ExecutionMutexAbortError` → mapped to `JobCancelledSentinel(queuedJournalId)` → existing cancelled pipeline → dApp 4001. The claim REUSES this controller (claimed id === queuedJournalId), so it's in `activeControllers` continuously from before the wait — strictly SAFER than the old "register only after the claim transition" timing (cancelJob always finds it). claim-helper edge: on the record-reaped→createFresh fallback the orphaned `queuedJournalId` controller entry is deleted (codex final-pass edge).
implementations-plan/dapp-interaction-lock-fix-v3/lessons/phase-0.md:44:1. **Slot-release leak.** `releaseSlot()` only ran in a `finally` that began AFTER claim + checkCancelled — both can throw on a raced cancel. A pre-`try` throw would wedge the (profileId,chainId) lane until SW restart once Phase 1 adds contention. Fix: hoisted `let journalId`, moved the claim + checkCancelled INSIDE the `try` whose `finally` releases the slot. Both paths.

implementations-plan/dapp-interaction-lock-fix-v3/audit-opus.md:38:The plan is right that `withPxeWrite` alone cannot keep T2 visibly Queued (nothing holds T2's journal stage). A real FIFO abortable mutex is easier to make cancel-correct and starvation-free than a journal-watch loop, and keying it to the chainGuard `(profileId, chainId)` makes the lock-order story trivially clean. **I withdraw the "no mutex" recommendation.** The plan won on engineering ergonomics. [And codex's falsification shows the mutex is outright correctness-required, not merely ergonomic.]
implementations-plan/dapp-interaction-lock-fix-v3/audit-opus.md:43:2. **Key `(profileId, chainId)` vs incl. account — agree, P2.** Per-account under-serializes: two accounts on one chain share the PXE runtime + chainGuard, so proving is already serialized at the runtime layer; a per-account exec-mutex would let two lifecycles overlap at the UX layer while the chainGuard silently serializes — the "both pending, one secretly blocked" confusion. `(profileId, chainId)` correct. (This reverses opus's own v2 take, which argued for incl. account.)
implementations-plan/dapp-interaction-lock-fix-v3/audit-opus.md:44:3. **Cancel-while-waiting (D5) lock order — P1.** During the wait there is NO controller for T2 (claim-helper registers the controller, and claim runs *after* acquire). So `cancelJob` finds no controller → not a deadlock but a **delayed cancel** (T2's promise doesn't reject until T1 finishes). Fix: register a pre-acquire AbortController keyed by `queuedJournalId` BEFORE `mutex.acquire`, thread its signal into acquire, claim-helper reuses it (claim-helper.ts:141 currently always `new AbortController()`). Lock order exec→journal consistent; no deadlock.

implementations-plan/dapp-interaction-lock-fix-v2/audit-opus.md:26:**[P1] "Per-account execution mutex" is underspecified.** Where does it live? `ExecutionService` is the natural owner, but `executeOperations` already lock-free fans through many op kinds. A new `Map<accountAddress, Lock>` in ExecutionService with eviction-on-leave semantics is the minimum. The plan also doesn't say what the lock key is — `accountAddress` alone or `(profileId, accountAddress, networkId)`? PR #53's `journalRecordInScope` filters by both `accountAddress` and `networkId`, so concurrent sendTx on the same account but different networks would currently surface fine; gating on `accountAddress` only would over-serialize. Use the tuple.
implementations-plan/dapp-interaction-lock-fix-v2/audit-opus.md:28:**[P1] Cancellation propagation through the new exec mutex is not specified.** Plan says "Cancel should still produce 4001 / JOB_CANCELLED at the dApp boundary. Pin in tests." But the mechanism isn't there: today `cancelJob` transitions the journal to `cancelled`, and `claimOrCreate` rechecks before claiming. With T2 *between* claim-helper's transition (queued → pending) and the new exec mutex's acquire, where does the cancel land? At minimum, T2 needs to `await mutex.acquire()` inside an `AbortSignal`-aware wrapper that throws `JobCancelledSentinel` if `controller.signal.aborted`. Add this to the plan or it will become a post-impl audit P0.
implementations-plan/dapp-interaction-lock-fix-v2/audit-opus.md:58:**Out-of-order popup approval.** User approves popup #2 *before* popup #1 (which is the parallel-popup model). T2's approveInteraction fires → T2's handler tries to acquire the per-account exec mutex → T1 still holds it. Now T1's user-facing popup is still open. Does the popup #1 approval landing later still cleanly Cancel T2's wait? The plan needs to spell out: T2's wait on the exec mutex is *cancellable* via T2's AbortController. When the user clicks "Cancel" on T2's queued card, `cancelJob` transitions T2 to `cancelled` AND aborts T2's controller → mutex.acquire() throws → JobCancelledSentinel → 4001. Spell this out explicitly in the plan.
implementations-plan/dapp-interaction-lock-fix-v2/audit-opus.md:70:- **Fee preset cache**: fee-method selection persists per `(profileId, networkId, accountAddress)` — the popup reads from `FeePreferencesService` on mount. If popup #1's user changes the fee preset before approving, popup #2 (opening later) inherits the new preset. **Behaviorally fine** — this is what the user just asked for. *But*: the dApp sees the new fee method on the second tx without warning. Worth a unit test.

audit/quality/2026-06-11-ultra-50b45d/raw/c6-rebuttal-claude.md:5:**codex-2 F4 (active-profile handoff temporal coupling) — WRONG, core mischaracterization.** The two helpers do not encode "one logical state change." `setSentinel()` takes no profileId and writes the build-defined `__SENTINEL__` constant (`packages/extension/src/utils/core.ts:141-149`, `vite.config.ts:312` — `packageJson.sentinel`); its only reader is `composables/notification.js:60-65`, which shows an "aztecReset" delete-your-profile notification when the stored stamp mismatches the build. It is a network-reset epoch marker, not activation state. `lastActiveProfile.ts:1-5` documents its own contract explicitly ("written whenever a profile becomes active (create / unlock / switch / import)"). The "partial pairing" codex cites as the smell (`auth.vue:101`, `SelectProfilePopup.vue:30` writing only the id) is correct by design — unlock/switch must not re-stamp a reset epoch. The proposed `markProfileActivated()` owning both writes would couple a reset marker to activation, making the code wronger. At most a 4-site creation-flow helper survives; the architectural bucket and "temporal coupling" mapping do not. Both Claude instances rejected this as a non-finding.
implementations-plan/registry-stealth-notes/audit-plan-agent-r2.md:103:### S4. PR 3 vitest `loadContractArtifact` risk is low but unverified
implementations-plan/registry-stealth-notes/audit-plan-agent-r2.md:105:Plan-v2 unit tests will load Wonderland Token/NFT/PrivateFPC JSON via the existing vite aliases (`vitest.config.ts:39-43`) and call `loadContractArtifact()`. **No existing test does this** (verified — `grep -rn "loadContractArtifact" packages --include="*.test.ts"` returns zero hits). The function uses `ContractArtifactSchema.parseAsync` (zod) plus `getContractClassFromArtifact` (poseidon hashing via `@aztec/foundation/crypto`). These should work in jsdom but it's a load-bearing assumption — first contact between vitest and `getContractClassFromArtifact`.

implementations-plan/backup-import-repair/plan.md:304:Codex caught that opening the session inside `restore()` triggers a race against auto-seed of default networks/accounts. The fix is a separate `finalizeRestore(profileId, password?)` RPC called after all backup data is restored. For passkey profiles, the SW retains the recovery secret in memory between `restore()` and `finalizeRestore()` to avoid a second WebAuthn prompt.

implementations-plan/M2/3/audit-codex.md:10:Plan keeps `ChainRuntimeRegistry` as effectively `Map<chainId, ChainRuntime>`, but real PXE namespace is `pxe/{profileId}/{chainId}` (service.ts:401) and `Network` carries `profileId` (spec.ts:11). implementations-plan/incoming-trust-state-machine-refactor/audit-codex.md:8:- **Ref-counted eviction is unsafe with `Lock` force-release.** `plan.md:47-54,413-417` assumes `releaseTripleLock(profileId, networkId, contract)` can safely look up the current map entry by key. It cannot once `Lock.enter()` can auto-`leave()` after 5 minutes (`packages/wallet-core/src/utils/lock.ts:37-43`). A timed-out holder can resume later, call `leave()` on the old lock object, then decrement/delete a newer lock instance recreated under the same key. Fix: have `withTripleLock` retain and release the exact entry object/token it acquired, or drop eviction unless `Lock` exposes a stable idle/ownership signal. Add a force-release + recreate regression.

implementations-plan/M2/README.md:3:> **M2.3 status (2026-04-22)**: COMPLETE — d/a/b/c shipped. Cut version 0.12.0. M2.3-d closed the real profile-switch read/write race (bounded registry fetch + reader counting + writer-FIFO drain + 5-min force-release). M2.3-a lifted per-chain state into `ChainRuntime`/`ChainRuntimeRegistry` keyed by (profileId, chainId) — also fixed a latent double-init bug by moving getOrInit inside `guard.read`. M2.3-b put artifact resolution behind an `ArtifactRegistry` with explicit policy + pinning + config.onUpdate subscription. M2.3-c hoisted the 20 `ensureOffscreenRunning` calls into the offscreen `ServiceClient` transport base via a template-method + hook. See per-sub-PR audit-diffs where they deviate from the plan.

implementations-plan/incoming-trust-state-machine-refactor/plan-opus.md:467:**OQ-4.** Should the lock map keys include `accountAddress` as well? Today the triple is `(profileId, networkId, contract)` — accountAddress is NOT in the key because trust is contract-scoped, not account-scoped. Records, however, are scoped by `(profileId, networkId, accountAddress, contract)`. Operations on records belonging to the same triple but different accounts (e.g., split-fee scenarios where account A's tx affects account B's record) still serialize via the contract-level lock — which is over-strict but correct. Open question: do we accept the false-sharing cost? **Default: yes**, the contract-level lock is fine. Account-add fanout under `onAccountAdded` doesn't write to the trust row; it just hydrates schedulers — not part of the critical section.

Triple key is (profileId, networkId, contract). All 8 writers (scanContract, setTrustState, setTrustAllow, setTrustReject, onTokenDeleted, onTransactionAdded, clearProfile, clearChain) funnel through withTriple/acquireMany helpers. Quality gates: bun lint, bun typecheck:all, bun test, bun test:e2e:network -- --testNamePattern=incoming-transfers all green. Branch refactor/incoming-transfer-triple-lock, 7-9 conventional commits (one per writer migration + tests + optional Lock.isIdle()). Single PR. implementations-plan/incoming-trust-state-machine-refactor/audit-codex-postimpl.md:6:`onActiveProfileChanged` now just calls `hydrateSchedulers()` and does not invalidate in-flight scans. On `dev`, `hydrateSchedulers()` explicitly bumped every scan generation before rebuild (`git show dev:packages/extension/src/wallet/services/incoming-transfer/service.ts:363-372`), so a scan parked before the rebuild would bail before mutating (`...:540-587`). In this branch, a scan for profile A that is parked on `getNotesRaw()` during an A→B switch can resume, pass the unchanged `serviceEpoch`, and still emit `onIncomingTransferAdded` for A. That is user-visible because the popup consumers blindly append/remove incoming-transfer events without checking the live `(profileId, networkId, accountAddress)` triple. Fix direction: treat active-profile scheduler rebuilds as lifecycle-cancel boundaries too. Bump `serviceEpoch` on profile-switch rehydrate and add a regression test that parks `getNotesRaw()` across A→B. Because the current UI listeners are unscoped, I would also harden the client-side `onIncomingTransferAdded` / `onIncomingTransferDeleted` handlers or route them through a triple filter.
implementations-plan/incoming-trust-state-machine-refactor/audit-codex-postimpl.md:9:`onAccountDeleted` scopes its record wipe through `getActiveProfile()` instead of the deleted account's own `profileId`. That is wrong for the two paths that emit `onAccountDeleted` for arbitrary profiles: chain purge and profile delete. If an inactive profile is being purged, this handler can delete incoming-transfer rows from the currently active profile when addresses overlap, and it can also tear down the active profile's scheduler entries because the scheduler key does not include `profileId`. Fix direction: accept the full `Account` payload here, use `account.profileId` for the repo wipe, and only touch `schedulers` / `watchedContracts` / `serviceEpoch` when the deleted account belongs to the active profile. Add a multi-profile regression test; the current coverage only checks scheduler removal on the active profile.

implementations-plan/security-audit-remediation/audit-codex.md:41:**Trace**: `implementations-plan/security-audit-remediation/plan.md:123-129,298-301` and `decision-ledger.md:128-140` choose a single `walletSdkSessionId?: string`. Current storage is one `DappSession` per `(origin, chainId, profileId)` (`packages/extension/src/wallet/services/dapp-session/service.ts:85-99`), but upstream can hold multiple live `ActiveSession`s keyed by `sessionId` (`node_modules/@aztec/wallet-sdk/src/extension/handlers/background_connection_handler.ts:167-170,290-301,412-417`). Returning-user discovery auto-approves new tabs against the same stored row (`packages/extension/src/wallet/services/wallet-sdk/background.ts:373-380`), and `onSessionEstablished` only looks up one stored row and writes `verificationHash` back to it (`:153-164`). Phase 5 then proposes frame-scoped session keying at `plan.md:156`.

implementations-plan/onboarding-fees-history-arc/audit-fixes-v2/audit-codex-final.md:4:- `plan.md:Load-bearing invariant` / `plan.md:P7` still misses the real load-bearing race: `reconcileTrust` gates on an initial `pending` read, then later writes `unknown` unconditionally. A concurrent user action can be clobbered. `setTrustAllow` / `setTrustReject` write immediately in [incoming-transfer/service.ts](/Users/alejoamiras/Projects/nulo/nulo-2/packages/extension/src/wallet/services/incoming-transfer/service.ts:226), while the planned reconcile writes later at [plan.md](/Users/alejoamiras/Projects/nulo/nulo-2/implementations-plan/onboarding-fees-history-arc/audit-fixes-v2/plan.md:327). Example: popup click `Allow` races journal/tx/hydrate reconcile; reconcile reads `pending`, user writes `trusted`, reconcile finishes and overwrites to `unknown`. Fix: add a per-`(profileId, networkId, contract)` lock or repo-level compare-and-set for `pending -> unknown`. Re-reading once before write is not enough without serialization.
implementations-plan/onboarding-fees-history-arc/audit-fixes-v2/audit-codex-final.md:11:- `plan.md:Profile Isolation` / `plan.md:P14` hand-waves away a real supported scenario. Same mnemonic / restored master key can absolutely yield the same Aztec address in two profiles because account derivation uses the profile secret, chain, type, and index, not `profileId` [account/service.ts](/Users/alejoamiras/Projects/nulo/nulo-2/packages/extension/src/wallet/services/account/service.ts:186); importing/restoring that secret is first-class [profile/service.ts](/Users/alejoamiras/Projects/nulo/nulo-2/packages/extension/src/wallet/services/profile/service.ts:598). Calling this “pathological” is indefensible. Worse, account rows are keyed by `address` [account/service.ts](/Users/alejoamiras/Projects/nulo/nulo-2/packages/extension/src/wallet/services/account/service.ts:23), so same-address cross-profile is a broader collision risk, not a thought experiment.
implementations-plan/onboarding-fees-history-arc/audit-fixes-v2/audit-codex-final.md:18:- `plan.md:Open questions` contains questions the repo already answers. `Tx` does not carry `profileId` [transaction/spec.ts](/Users/alejoamiras/Projects/nulo/nulo-2/packages/extension/src/wallet/services/transaction/spec.ts:91). `onOperationUpdated` can fire without a stage transition because `setOperationMeta` emits it [operation-journal/service.ts](/Users/alejoamiras/Projects/nulo/nulo-2/packages/extension/src/wallet/services/operation-journal/service.ts:321). That drift is a smell: this plan is still asking the codebase questions it could have closed.
implementations-plan/onboarding-fees-history-arc/audit-fixes-v2/audit-codex-post-impl-fixups.md:5:  The new live-triple guard closes the async emit ingress only. All replay paths, including the watcher-fired `tryReplayForTriple()`, still eventually emit `onIncomingTransferPending`, so there is no second queue ingress bypassing the guard. But High #1 is still not fully closed because stale payloads already accepted before an identity switch remain live: `dequeueNextPendingTrust()` blindly opens whatever is already in `pendingTrustQueue`, and the triple watcher only replays, it never purges or auto-closes stale popup state. Concrete repro: queue/open A payload(s), switch to B, then close the current trust popup; the next queued A payload still opens under B. Fix: on `(profileId, networkId, accountAddress)` change, drop queued payloads whose triple no longer matches, close/clear an open `incoming_trust` popup if stale, and make `dequeueNextPendingTrust()` skip mismatched entries defensively.
implementations-plan/e2e-full-network-recovery/audit-opus.md:159:| **PXE-CREATE-START** | `packages/aztec-runtime/src/pxe/chain-runtime.ts` | line 75 (inside `createChainRuntime`, before `createPXE(...)`) | `{ chainId, profileId, t }` |
implementations-plan/e2e-full-network-recovery/audit-opus.md:186:**Why this works**: `createPXE` for a specific (profileId, chainId) is still lazy (done on first network-touching call). But the *cold-cache JS/WASM cost* is paid once on SW boot, not on first user network-switch. A first-switch then triggers `createPXE` against a warm import graph in 2-3s instead of 30s.
implementations-plan/e2e-full-network-recovery/audit-opus.md:198:**Why second**: more work than F-B1 because we need to teach the SW about what "the user's active network" is at boot time (read `nulo:core:active-network@<profileId>` from storage). Also runs PXE op for an unspecified network — fine for active network, but feels overreach-y if there are multiple profiles.
implementations-plan/e2e-full-network-recovery/audit-opus.md:279:**Threat**: F-B1 (pre-warm offscreen modules at SW boot) doesn't talk to any network RPC. Confirmed safe — no privacy leak. F-B2 (pre-create PXE for active network) creates an in-memory PXE bound to user's profileId + chainId; PXE doesn't auto-sync without an op being called against it, so still no leak. F-B3 (popup-side) is same as F-B2 timing-wise.
implementations-plan/e2e-full-network-recovery/audit-opus.md:295:The `E2E_REQUIRE_SETUP=1` env gate (added in this branch) only affects the test harness's exit code. Probes (this plan) gate on Vite `define` constants that compile-time eliminate. No test-only code paths ship to prod.

implementations-plan/bundle-fpc-nft/audit-codex.md:1164:81:      "source": "//! The `self` contract value for public execution contexts.\n\nuse crate::{\n    context::{calls::{PublicCall, PublicStaticCall}, PublicContext},\n    event::{event_emission::emit_event_in_public, event_interface::EventInterface},\n};\nuse crate::protocol::{address::AztecAddress, traits::{Deserialize, Serialize}};\n\n/// Core interface for interacting with aztec-nr contract features in public execution contexts.\n///\n/// This struct is automatically injected into every [`external`](crate::macros::functions::external) and\n/// [`internal`](crate::macros::functions::internal) contract function marked with `\"public\"` by the Aztec macro\n/// system and is accessible through the `self` variable.\n///\n/// ## Type Parameters\n///\n/// - `Storage`: The contract's storage struct (defined with [`storage`](crate::macros::storage::storage), or `()` if\n/// the contract has no storage\n/// - `CallSelf`: Macro-generated type for calling contract's own non-view functions\n/// - `CallSelfStatic`: Macro-generated type for calling contract's own view functions\n/// - `CallInternal`: Macro-generated type for calling internal functions\npub struct ContractSelfPublic<Storage, CallSelf, CallSelfStatic, CallInternal> {\n    /// The address of this contract\n    pub address: AztecAddress,\n\n    /// The contract's storage instance, representing the struct to which the\n    /// [`storage`](crate::macros::storage::storage) macro was applied in your contract. If the contract has no\n    /// storage, the type of this will be `()`.\n    ///\n    /// This storage instance is specialized for the current execution context (public) and\n    /// provides access to the contract's state variables.\n    ///\n    /// ## Developer Note\n    ///\n    /// If you've arrived here while trying to access your contract's storage while the `Storage` generic type is set\n    /// to unit type `()`, it means you haven't yet defined a Storage struct using the\n    /// [`storage`](crate::macros::storage::storage) macro in your contract. For guidance on setting this up, please\n    /// refer to our docs: https://docs.aztec.network/developers/docs/guides/smart_contracts/storage\n    pub storage: Storage,\n\n    /// The public execution context.\n    pub context: PublicContext,\n\n    /// Provides type-safe methods for calling this contract's own non-view functions.\n    ///\n    /// Example API:\n    /// ```noir\n    /// self.call_self.some_public_function(args)\n    /// ```\n    pub call_self: CallSelf,\n\n    /// Provides type-safe methods for calling this contract's own view functions.\n    ///\n    /// Example API:\n    /// ```noir\n    /// self.call_self_static.some_view_function(args)\n    /// ```\n    pub call_self_static: CallSelfStatic,\n\n    /// Provides type-safe methods for calling internal functions.\n    ///\n    /// Example API:\n    /// ```noir\n    /// self.internal.some_internal_function(args)\n    /// ```\n    pub internal: CallInternal,\n}\n\nimpl<Storage, CallSelf, CallSelfStatic, CallInternal> ContractSelfPublic<Storage, CallSelf, CallSelfStatic, CallInternal> {\n    /// Creates a new `ContractSelfPublic` instance for a public function.\n    ///\n    /// This constructor is called automatically by the macro system and should not be called directly.\n    pub fn new(\n        context: PublicContext,\n        storage: Storage,\n        call_self: CallSelf,\n        call_self_static: CallSelfStatic,\n        internal: CallInternal,\n    ) -> Self {\n        Self { context, storage, address: context.this_address(), call_self, call_self_static, internal }\n    }\n\n    /// The address of the contract address that made this function call.\n    ///\n    /// This is similar to Solidity's `msg.sender` value.\n    ///\n    /// ## Incognito Calls\n    ///\n    /// Contracts can call public functions from private ones hiding their identity (see\n    ///\n    /// [`ContractSelfPrivate::enqueue_incognito`](crate::contract_self::ContractSelfPrivate::enqueue_incognito)).\n    /// This function reverts when executed in such a context.\n    ///\n    /// If you need to handle these cases, use [`PublicContext::maybe_msg_sender`].\n    pub fn msg_sender(self: Self) -> AztecAddress {\n        self.context.maybe_msg_sender().unwrap()\n    }\n\n    /// Emits an event publicly.\n    ///\n    /// Public events are emitted as plaintext and are therefore visible to everyone. This is is the same as Solidity\n    /// events on EVM chains.\n    ///\n    /// Unlike private events, they don't require delivery of an event message.\n    ///\n    /// # Example\n    /// ```noir\n    /// #[event]\n    /// struct Update { value: Field }\n    ///\n    /// #[external(\"public\")]\n    /// fn publish_update(value: Field) {\n    ///     self.emit(Update { value });\n    /// }\n    /// ```\n    ///\n    /// # Cost\n    ///\n    /// Public event emission is achieved by emitting public transaction logs. A total of `N+1` fields are emitted,\n    /// where `N` is the serialization length of the event.\n    pub fn emit<Event>(&mut self, event: Event)\n    where\n        Event: EventInterface + Serialize,\n    {\n        emit_event_in_public(self.context, event);\n    }\n\n    /// Makes a public contract call.\n    ///\n    /// Will revert if the called function reverts or runs out of gas.\n    ///\n    /// # Arguments\n    /// * `call` - The object representing the public function to invoke.\n    ///\n    /// # Returns\n    /// * `T` - Whatever data the called function has returned.\n    ///\n    /// # Example\n    /// ```noir\n    /// self.call(Token::at(address).transfer_in_public(recipient, amount));\n    /// ```\n    ///\n    pub unconstrained fn call<let M: u32, let N: u32, T>(self, call: PublicCall<M, N, T>) -> T\n    where\n        T: Deserialize,\n    {\n        call.call(self.context)\n    }\n\n    /// Makes a public read-only contract call.\n    ///\n    /// This is similar to Solidity's `staticcall`. The called function cannot modify state or emit events. Any nested\n    /// calls are constrained to also be static calls.\n    ///\n    /// Will revert if the called function reverts or runs out of gas.\n    ///\n    /// # Arguments\n    /// * `call` - The object representing the read-only public function to invoke.\n    ///\n    /// # Returns\n    /// * `T` - Whatever data the called function has returned.\n    ///\n    /// # Example\n    /// ```noir\n    /// self.view(Token::at(address).balance_of_public(recipient));\n    /// ```\n    ///\n    pub unconstrained fn view<let M: u32, let N: u32, T>(self, call: PublicStaticCall<M, N, T>) -> T\n    where\n        T: Deserialize,\n    {\n        call.view(self.context)\n    }\n}\n"
implementations-plan/bundle-fpc-nft/audit-codex.md:1167:501:      "source": "pub mod types;\npub mod test;\n\nuse aztec::macros::aztec;\n\n#[aztec]\npub contract NFT {\n    // aztec library\n    use aztec::{\n        authwit::auth::{\n            assert_current_call_valid_authwit, assert_current_call_valid_authwit_public,\n        },\n        context::PrivateContext,\n        macros::{\n            events::event,\n            functions::{external, initializer, internal, only_self, view},\n            storage::storage,\n        },\n        messages::message_delivery::MessageDelivery,\n        note::{\n            constants::MAX_NOTES_PER_PAGE, note_getter_options::NoteGetterOptions,\n            note_interface::NoteProperties, note_viewer_options::NoteViewerOptions,\n        },\n        protocol::{address::AztecAddress, traits::{FromField, ToField}},\n        state_vars::{Map, Owned, PrivateSet, PublicImmutable, PublicMutable, StateVariable},\n        utils::comparison::Comparator,\n    };\n    // compression library\n    use compressed_string::FieldCompressedString;\n    // nft note structs\n    use crate::types::nft_note::{NFTNote, PartialNFTNote};\n\n    /// @param symbol The symbol of the NFT\n    /// @param name The name of the NFT\n    /// @param private_nfts A map from address to a private set of NFTNotes owned by that address\n    /// @param nft_exists A map from token ID to a boolean indicating if the NFT exists\n    /// @param public_owners A map from token ID to the public owner of the NFT\n    /// @param minter The address that can mint\n    #[storage]\n    struct Storage<Context> {\n        symbol: PublicImmutable<FieldCompressedString, Context>,\n        name: PublicImmutable<FieldCompressedString, Context>,\n        private_nfts: Owned<PrivateSet<NFTNote, Context>, Context>,\n        nft_exists: Map<Field, PublicMutable<bool, Context>, Context>,\n        public_owners: Map<Field, PublicMutable<AztecAddress, Context>, Context>,\n        minter: PublicImmutable<AztecAddress, Context>,\n    }\n\n    // Sentinel address used in Transfer events to represent the private side of a balance change.\n    // sha224sum 'PRIVATE_ADDRESS'\n    global PRIVATE_ADDRESS_MAGIC_VALUE: AztecAddress =\n        AztecAddress::from_field(0x1ea7e01501975545617c2e694d931cb576b691a4a867fed81ebd3264);\n\n    #[event]\n    struct Transfer {\n        from: AztecAddress,\n        to: AztecAddress,\n        token_id: Field,\n    }\n\n    /// @dev Initializes the token with a minter\n    /// @param name The name of the NFT\n    /// @param symbol The symbol of the NFT\n    /// @param minter The address of the minter\n    #[external(\"public\")]\n    #[initializer]\n    fn constructor_with_minter(name: str<31>, symbol: str<31>, minter: AztecAddress) {\n        self.storage.name.initialize(FieldCompressedString::from_string(name));\n        self.storage.symbol.initialize(FieldCompressedString::from_string(symbol));\n        self.storage.minter.initialize(minter);\n    }\n\n    /** ==========================================================\n     * ========================= PRIVATE =========================\n     * ======================================================== */\n\n    /// @notice Transfers token by id from private owner to a public owner\n    /// @dev Removes token from private owner, and enqueues a public call to update the public owner\n    /// @param from The address of the sender\n    /// @param to The address of the recipient\n    /// @param token_id The id of the token to transfer\n    /// @param _nonce The nonce used for authwitness\n    #[external(\"private\")]\n    fn transfer_private_to_public(\n        from: AztecAddress,\n        to: AztecAddress,\n        token_id: Field,\n        _nonce: Field,\n    ) {\n        _validate_from_private::<4>(self.context, from);\n\n        self.internal._remove_private_token_owner(from, token_id);\n        self.enqueue_self.update_public_token_owner_from_zero_internal(to, token_id);\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Transfers token by id from private owner to a public owner with a commitment\n    /// @dev Removes token from private owner, enqueues a public call to update the public owner, and returns a commitment\n    /// @param from The address of the sender\n    /// @param to The address of the recipient\n    /// @param token_id The id of the token to transfer\n    /// @param _nonce The nonce used for authwitness\n    /// @return commitment The partial nft note utilized for the transfer commitment (privacy entrance)\n    #[external(\"private\")]\n    fn transfer_private_to_public_with_commitment(\n        from: AztecAddress,\n        to: AztecAddress,\n        token_id: Field,\n        _nonce: Field,\n    ) -> Field {\n        _validate_from_private::<4>(self.context, from);\n\n        self.internal._remove_private_token_owner(from, token_id);\n        self.enqueue_self.update_public_token_owner_from_zero_internal(to, token_id);\n        let completer = self.msg_sender();\n        let commitment = self.internal._initialize_transfer_commitment(to, completer);\n        commitment.commitment\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Transfers token by id from private owner to another private owner\n    /// @dev Removes token by id from private owner, and sends a nft note with id to the recipient\n    /// @param from The address of the sender\n    /// @param to The address of the recipient\n    /// @param token_id The id of the token to transfer\n    /// @param _nonce The nonce used for authwitness\n    #[external(\"private\")]\n    fn transfer_private_to_private(\n        from: AztecAddress,\n        to: AztecAddress,\n        token_id: Field,\n        _nonce: Field,\n    ) {\n        _validate_from_private::<4>(self.context, from);\n\n        self.internal._remove_private_token_owner(from, token_id);\n        self.internal._update_private_token_owner(to, token_id);\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Transfers token by id from private owner to the recipient commitment (recipient must create a commitment first)\n    /// @dev Removes token by id from private owner, and enqueues a public call to complete the commitment\n    /// @param from The address of the sender\n    /// @param token_id The id of the token to transfer\n    /// @param commitment The commitment to use for the transfer\n    /// @param _nonce The nonce used for authwitness\n    #[external(\"private\")]\n    fn transfer_private_to_commitment(\n        from: AztecAddress,\n        token_id: Field,\n        commitment: Field,\n        _nonce: Field,\n    ) {\n        _validate_from_private::<4>(self.context, from);\n\n        self.internal._remove_private_token_owner(from, token_id);\n        let completer = from;\n        self.enqueue_self.transfer_token_to_commitment_internal(\n            commitment.to_field(),\n            token_id,\n            completer,\n        );\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Transfers token by id from public owner to private owner\n    /// @dev Enqueues a public call to remove the public owner, and emits a nft note with id to the recipient\n    /// @param from The address of the sender\n    /// @param to The address of the recipient\n    /// @param token_id The id of the token to transfer\n    /// @param _nonce The nonce used for authwitness\n    #[external(\"private\")]\n    fn transfer_public_to_private(\n        from: AztecAddress,\n        to: AztecAddress,\n        token_id: Field,\n        _nonce: Field,\n    ) {\n        _validate_from_private::<4>(self.context, from);\n\n        self.enqueue_self.transfer_public_to_private_internal(from, token_id);\n        self.internal._update_private_token_owner(to, token_id);\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Initializes a transfer commitment to be used for transfers\n    /// @dev Returns a partial nft note that can be used to execute transfers\n    /// @param to The address of the recipient\n    /// @param completer The address allowed to complete the partial note\n    /// @return commitment The partial nft note utilized for the transfer commitment (privacy entrance)\n    #[external(\"private\")]\n    fn initialize_transfer_commitment(to: AztecAddress, completer: AztecAddress) -> Field {\n        let commitment = self.internal._initialize_transfer_commitment(to, completer);\n        commitment.commitment\n    }\n\n    /** ==========================================================\n     * ========================= PUBLIC ==========================\n     * ======================================================== */\n\n    /// @notice Transfers a token from one public owner to another public owner\n    /// @dev Public call that asserts that the caller is the token owner, and updates the public owner\n    /// @param from The address of the sender\n    /// @param to The address of the recipient\n    /// @param token_id The id of the token to transfer\n    /// @param _nonce The nonce used for authwitness\n    #[external(\"public\")]\n    fn transfer_public_to_public(\n        from: AztecAddress,\n        to: AztecAddress,\n        token_id: Field,\n        _nonce: Field,\n    ) {\n        self.internal._validate_from_public(from);\n implementations-plan/onboarding-fees-history-arc/audit-fixes-v2/audit-opus.md:33:P7 (plan.md:284-287) says the journal handler "find[s] any records with that `(profileId, networkId, txHash)` triple; delete each + reconcile". `IncomingTransferRepository.listByTxHash(profile.id, network.id, tx.hash)` is the existing API (called at `service.ts:374`). But journal records carry `(profileId, networkId, accountAddress)` triples. A record matching the journal's txHash but belonging to a DIFFERENT accountAddress would still be deleted under the plan's pseudo-code — even though the journal op was fired by account A and the matching incoming record belongs to account B.
