implementations-plan/onboarding-fees-history-arc/audit-fixes/audit-opus.md:28:- **P5 `hydrateSchedulers()` on every `onAccountAdded` is overkill** — Plan §P5 line 118 proposes `accountService.onAccountAdded → hydrateSchedulers()`. Looking at the implementation at `service.ts:242-264`, `hydrateSchedulers` calls `clearInterval` on every existing scheduler, wipes the maps, then iterates ALL networks × ALL accounts × all tokens and re-spins each scheduler from scratch. Single-account-add fires this entire teardown for every other account/network on the profile. For a profile with 5 accounts × 3 networks × 10 tokens, that's 15 schedulers torn down and re-built every time the user clicks "+ New Account". The right shape: an additive `startScheduler(profileId, network.id, account.address)` per existing token list (mirroring the `onTokenAdded` handler at `service.ts:282-301`), plus a more surgical `onAccountDeleted` that only tears down the deleted account's schedulers. The plan's stated rationale "trade-offs" at the bottom of §P5 is a hand-wave — write down which one was picked and why. If `hydrateSchedulers` is chosen for simplicity, the plan should justify that the rebuild cost is bounded (no PXE calls inside, schedulers don't trigger immediate polls except for newly-registered keys). The cost is real though: every scheduler `startScheduler` triggers an immediate `poll()` per `service.ts:277-279`, so even an "idempotent re-build" causes a full PXE scan storm whenever any account is added/deleted.
implementations-plan/onboarding-fees-history-arc/audit-fixes/audit-opus.md:32:- **P4 "toggle off → on re-emit" subscription is correctly bundled but needs failure-mode spec** — Plan §3 line 205-206 says "when toggle flips back ON, `replayPendingPrompts` should run. Add a config-change subscription in `IncomingTransferService`". Yes, this belongs in P4 — but the plan doesn't pin WHICH `(profileId, networkId, accountAddress)` triple to replay for. There's no implicit "active profile / network / account" in `IncomingTransferService`; the existing `onActiveProfileChanged` handler at `service.ts:142-144` just hydrates schedulers. The new config-toggle handler would need access to the same triple — either by re-deriving from `profileService.getActiveProfile()` + `networkService.getActiveNetwork()` + `accountService.getActiveAccount()` (none of which the service currently calls), OR by emitting a service event that the POPUP-side subscriber re-fires `replayPendingPrompts` against the popup's appStore values. The latter is the more honest design (service is per-profile, popup knows the active triple). Plan should spell this out — as written, "add a config-change subscription" is ambiguous.
implementations-plan/faucet-add-token/audit-opus.md:36:**H2** — `executeRegisterToken` is NOT DoS-safe. Each call hits `parseTokenInterface` (PXE round-trip) AND writes a `token_import` journal entry (`token/service.ts:133`) BEFORE the idempotency check at line 149. A malicious dApp can flood `registerToken(account, RANDOM_ADDR)` → unbounded PXE traffic + journal growth. Idempotency only helps for re-adds of the same address, not new junk. Mitigation: short-circuit before journal writes if `findToken(profileId, chainId, contract)` succeeds (already-known); add a soft rate-limit (e.g. drop attempts after N pending PXE parses for the same session).
implementations-plan/faucet-add-token/audit-opus.md:54:**M4** — Per-(profileId, chainId) scoping correct, but missing edge case: `parseTokenInterface(networkId, ...)` could return a `chainId` from the wallet's mismatched network if the dApp's chain isn't in the wallet's registry. Add a test: registerToken for chain-X token while session is on chain-Y → should refuse rather than register under wrong chain.

   151			const task = this.taskService.startNewTask(new StepContent(`${enabled ? "Enable" : "Disable"} auth registry`))
   152			try {
   153				const txHash = await this.executionService.executeSendTransaction(
   154					{
   155						kind: "send_transaction",
   156						networkId,
   157						accountAddress: account,
   158						feeSettings,
   159						actions: [
   160							{
   161								kind: "call",
   162								contract: getAuthRegistryAddress().toString(),
   163								method: "set_reject_all",
   164								args: [!enabled],
   165							},
   166						],
   167					},
   168					{ type: OriginType.UI },
   169					task,
   170				)
   171	
   172				await this.transactionService.waitForTx(txHash, task)
   173	
   174				const network = await this.networkService.getNetwork(networkId)
   175				const node = await this.networkService.getNode(network.chainId)
   176				await this.syncStatus(node, account, task)
   177	
   178				task.complete()
   179			} catch (error) {
   180				// Convert the internal sentinel to the structured RPC-boundary
   181				// error so the popup's `classifyCancellableRejection` works.
   182				// Same conversion done by `executeTransfer`.
   183				maybeRethrowAsRpcCancel(error, task)
   184				task.fail(error)
   185				throw error
   186			}
   187		}
   188	
   189		public async syncRegistry(networkId: string, account: string): Promise<void> {
   190			await this.ensureInitialized()
   191			const task = this.taskService.startNewTask(new StepContent("Sync auth registry"))
   192			try {
   193				const network = await this.networkService.getNetwork(networkId)
   194				const node = await this.networkService.getNode(network.chainId)
   195				await Promise.all([this.syncAuthwits(node, account, task), this.syncStatus(node, account, task)])
   196				task.complete()
   197			} catch (error) {
   198				task.fail(error)
   199				throw error
   200			}
   201		}
   202	
   203		private async syncAuthwits(node: AztecNode, account: string, parentTask: WrappedTask, authwits?: Authwit[]) {
   204			const task = parentTask.startSubtask(new StepContent("Sync authwits"))
   205			try {
   206				const _authwits = authwits ?? (await this.getAuthwits(account))
   207				await Promise.all(_authwits.map((authwit) => this.syncAuthwit(node, authwit, task)))
   208				task.complete()
   209			} catch (error) {
   210				task.fail(error)
   211				throw error
   212			}
   213		}
   214	
   215		private async syncAuthwit(node: AztecNode, authwit: Authwit, parentTask: WrappedTask) {
   216			const task = parentTask.startSubtask(new StepContent(`Sync authwit #${authwit.id}`))
   217			try {
   218				const isConsumable = await isAuthwitConsumable(node, authwit.account, authwit.hash)
   219				if (isConsumable) return
   220				try {
   221					await this.lock.enter()
   222					if (await this.authwits.get(`${authwit.id}`)) {
   223						await this.authwits.delete(`${authwit.id}`)
   224						this.emit("onAuthwitDeleted", authwit)
   225					}
   226				} finally {
   227					this.lock.leave()
   228				}
   229				task.complete()
   230			} catch (error) {
   231				task.fail(error)
   232				throw error
   233			}
   234		}
   235	
   236		private async syncStatus(node: AztecNode, account: string, parentTask: WrappedTask): Promise<void> {
   237			const task = parentTask.startSubtask(new StepContent("Sync status"))
   238			try {
   239				const isEnabled = await isAuthRegistryEnabled(node, account)
   240				try {
   241					await this.lock.enter()
   242					const enabled = await this.statuses.get(account)
   243					if (enabled !== isEnabled) {
   244						if (isEnabled) {
   245							await this.statuses.delete(account)
   246							this.emit("onRegistryEnabled", account)
   247						} else {
   248							await this.statuses.set(account, isEnabled)
   249							this.emit("onRegistryDisabled", account)
   250						}
   251					}
   252				} finally {
   253					this.lock.leave()
   254				}
   255				task.complete()
   256			} catch (error) {
   257				task.fail(error)
   258				throw error
   259			}
   260		}

    44	 *  Aztec deps) and pointless for tests that don't touch the faucet. */
    45	const FAUCET_PORT = process.env.FAUCET_DEV_PORT ? Number(process.env.FAUCET_DEV_PORT) : undefined
    46	const FAUCET_URL = FAUCET_PORT ? `http://localhost:${FAUCET_PORT}/` : undefined
    47	
    48	/** Per-run aztec data directory. Mandatory even for in-memory mode because
    49	 *  some aztec subsystems still write to ~/.aztec/data by default — two
    50	 *  agents writing there at the same time will corrupt LMDB. The path is
    51	 *  recorded in the ownership lockfile so a future run can clean it up
    52	 *  if this run is killed before teardown. */
    53	let AZTEC_DATA_DIR = path.join(tmpdir(), `nulo-aztec-${process.pid}-${Date.now()}`)
    54	
    55	let anvilProcess: ChildProcess | null = null
    56	let weStartedAnvil = false
    57	let nodeProcess: ChildProcess | null = null
    58	let weStartedNode = false
    59	let playgroundProcess: ChildProcess | null = null
    60	let weStartedPlayground = false
    61	let faucetProcess: ChildProcess | null = null
    62	let weStartedFaucet = false
    63	
    64	/** Probe a URL with HEAD/GET; returns true on any 2xx/3xx/4xx response. */
    65	async function probeHttp(url: string, timeoutMs = 1500): Promise<boolean> {
    66		return new Promise((resolve) => {
    67			const req = http.get(url, { timeout: timeoutMs }, (res) => {
    68				res.resume() // drain
    69				resolve((res.statusCode ?? 0) > 0)
    70			})
    71			req.on("error", () => resolve(false))
    72			req.on("timeout", () => {
    73				req.destroy()
    74				resolve(false)
    75			})
    76		})
    77	}
    78	
    79	async function waitForHttp(url: string, timeoutMs = 30_000): Promise<void> {
    80		const start = Date.now()
    81		while (Date.now() - start < timeoutMs) {
    82			if (await probeHttp(url)) return
    83			await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 500))
    84		}
    85		throw new Error(`Timed out waiting for ${url} (${timeoutMs}ms)`)
    86	}
    87	
    88	/** Single-shot anvil JSON-RPC eth_blockNumber probe. Confirms the L1 is
    89	 *  speaking JSON-RPC, not just answering HTTP. */
    90	async function probeAnvil(url: string, timeoutMs = 1500): Promise<boolean> {
    91		return new Promise((resolve) => {
    92			const u = new URL(url)
    93			const req = http.request(
    94				{
    95					hostname: u.hostname,
    96					port: u.port,
    97					path: "/",
    98					method: "POST",
    99					headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
   100					timeout: timeoutMs,
   101				},
   102				(res) => {
   103					let body = ""
   104					res.on("data", (c) => {
   105						body += c.toString()
   106					})
   107					res.on("end", () => {
   108						try {
   109							const parsed = JSON.parse(body)
   110							resolve(typeof parsed.result === "string")
   111						} catch {
   112							resolve(false)
   113						}
   114					})
   115				},
   116			)
   117			req.on("error", () => resolve(false))
   118			req.on("timeout", () => {
   119				req.destroy()
   120				resolve(false)
   121			})
   122			req.write(JSON.stringify({ jsonrpc: "2.0", id: 1, method: "eth_blockNumber", params: [] }))
   123			req.end()
   124		})
   125	}
   126	
   127	async function waitForAnvil(url: string, timeoutMs = 30_000): Promise<void> {
   128		const start = Date.now()
   129		while (Date.now() - start < timeoutMs) {
   130			if (await probeAnvil(url)) return
   131			await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 250))
   132		}
   133		throw new Error(`Timed out waiting for anvil at ${url} (${timeoutMs}ms)`)
   134	}
   135	
   136	/**
   137	 * Kill orphan Chrome test processes started by THIS extension build only.
   138	 *
   139	 * Scoping by extension path (not just `--test-type`) lets a parallel impl in
   140	 * a different folder run its own Chromes without us murdering each other's
   141	 * test runs.
   142	 */
   143	function killOrphanChromes() {
   144		try {
   145			execSync(`pkill -f "chrome.*--load-extension=${EXTENSION_PATH}" 2>/dev/null || true`, { stdio: "ignore" })
   146		} catch {}
   147	}
   148	
   149	export default async function setup(project: TestProject) {
   150		killOrphanChromes()
   151	
   152		// Guard: ensure extension is built
   153		const manifest = path.join(EXTENSION_PATH, "manifest.json")
   154		if (!fs.existsSync(manifest)) {
   155			throw new Error(`Extension not found at ${EXTENSION_PATH}\nRun "bun run build" or "bun run dev" first.`)
   156		}
   157		project.provide("extensionPath", EXTENSION_PATH)
   158	
   159		console.log(
   160			`[e2e-setup] ports: anvil=:${ANVIL_PORT} aztec=:${AZTEC_PORT} (admin :${AZTEC_ADMIN_PORT}, p2p :${AZTEC_P2P_PORT}) playground=:${PLAYGROUND_PORT}`,
   161		)
   162	
   163		// ── Lockfile: reap orphans or take over a still-healthy pack ───────
   164		// `bun run e2e:agent` always allocates fresh ports, so the prior lock's
   165		// ports never match the current ones — we fall through to reaping
   166		// orphans, then a fresh spawn. Direct vitest invocations with stable
   167		// env can land on the reuse path.
   168		const priorLock = readLock()
   169		if (priorLock) {
   170			const portsMatch =
   171				priorLock.ports.anvil === ANVIL_PORT &&
   172				priorLock.ports.aztec === AZTEC_PORT &&
   173				priorLock.ports.aztecAdmin === AZTEC_ADMIN_PORT &&
   174				priorLock.ports.aztecP2P === AZTEC_P2P_PORT &&
   175				priorLock.ports.playground === PLAYGROUND_PORT &&
   176				// Faucet port is optional — match only if both sides agree on its
   177				// presence and value. Lockfiles written before faucet wiring have
   178				// `priorLock.ports.faucet === undefined`; current runs without
   179				// faucet have `FAUCET_PORT === undefined`. Both match.
   180				priorLock.ports.faucet === FAUCET_PORT
   181			const urlMatch = priorLock.bakedLocalRpcUrl === LOCAL_NODE_URL
   182			if (portsMatch && urlMatch) {
   183				console.log("[e2e-setup] prior ownership lock matches current run — probing for reuse")
   184				const allCoreAlive =
   185					isPidAlive(priorLock.pids.anvil) && isPidAlive(priorLock.pids.aztec) && isPidAlive(priorLock.pids.playground)
   186				const faucetAlive = FAUCET_PORT ? isPidAlive(priorLock.pids.faucet) : true
   187				const faucetHealthy = FAUCET_URL ? await probeHttp(FAUCET_URL) : true
   188				const allHealthy =
   189					allCoreAlive &&
   190					faucetAlive &&
   191					(await probeAnvil(ANVIL_URL)) &&
   192					(await checkNodeHealth(LOCAL_NODE_URL)) &&
   193					(await probeHttp(PLAYGROUND_URL)) &&
   194					faucetHealthy
   195				if (allHealthy) {
   196					const identityOk = await verifyIdentity(LOCAL_NODE_URL, priorLock.l1ContractAddresses)
   197					if (identityOk) {
   198						console.log("[e2e-setup] reusing prior sandbox (identity check passed)")
   199						weStartedAnvil = false
   200						weStartedNode = false
   201						weStartedPlayground = false
   202						weStartedFaucet = false
   203						AZTEC_DATA_DIR = priorLock.aztecDataDir
   204						project.provide("playgroundUrl", PLAYGROUND_URL)
   205						project.provide("faucetUrl", FAUCET_URL)
   206						await deployContractsAndProvide(project)
   207						return
   208					}
   209					console.warn("[e2e-setup] prior sandbox identity mismatch — tearing down and starting fresh")
   210				} else {
   211					console.warn("[e2e-setup] prior sandbox not all healthy — tearing down")
   212				}
   213				killOrphanByPid(priorLock.pids.anvil, "anvil")
   214				killOrphanByPid(priorLock.pids.aztec, "aztec")
   215				killOrphanByPid(priorLock.pids.playground, "playground")
   216				killOrphanByPid(priorLock.pids.faucet, "faucet")
   217				try {
   218					fs.rmSync(priorLock.aztecDataDir, { recursive: true, force: true })
   219				} catch {}
   220			} else {
   221				// Different ports — fresh agent run after a previous one in the
   222				// same worktree. Reap any orphans on the previous ports.
   223				console.log("[e2e-setup] prior lock is for different ports — reaping orphans")
   224				killOrphanByPid(priorLock.pids.anvil, "anvil")
   225				killOrphanByPid(priorLock.pids.aztec, "aztec")
   226				killOrphanByPid(priorLock.pids.playground, "playground")
   227				killOrphanByPid(priorLock.pids.faucet, "faucet")
   228				try {
   229					fs.rmSync(priorLock.aztecDataDir, { recursive: true, force: true })
   230				} catch {}
   231			}
   232			clearLock()
   233		}
   234	
   235		// ── Anvil (L1) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   236		const anvilAlreadyRunning = await probeAnvil(ANVIL_URL)
   237		if (anvilAlreadyRunning) {
   238			console.log("[e2e-setup] Anvil already speaking JSON-RPC at", ANVIL_URL)
   239			weStartedAnvil = false
   240		} else {
   241			if (!fs.existsSync(ANVIL_BIN)) {
   242				// Same fail-loud gate as the deploy-failure path below: when invoked
   243				// via scripts/e2e/agent.sh, missing infrastructure must abort the
   244				// run, not pass-by-skip. Otherwise CI reports `61 skipped` exit 0
   245				// and the suite stays silently broken (this regressed in CI from
   246				// 2026-05-22 when the setup-aztec action didn't symlink
   247				// ~/.aztec/current — every PR's network-e2e check was "green" while
   248				// running zero tests).
   249				if (process.env.E2E_REQUIRE_SETUP === "1") {
   250					throw new Error(
   251						`[e2e-setup] FATAL: anvil binary not found at ${ANVIL_BIN} and E2E_REQUIRE_SETUP=1 is set. ` +
   252							`Aborting run to prevent silent pass-by-skip. Ensure setup-aztec installed Aztec CLI ` +
   253							`AND created the ~/.aztec/current symlink (CI: see .github/actions/setup-aztec/action.yml).`,
   254					)
   255				}
   256				console.warn("[e2e-setup] anvil binary not found at", ANVIL_BIN, "— skipping network setup")
   257				project.provide("aztecTestConfig", undefined)
   258				project.provide("playgroundUrl", PLAYGROUND_URL)
   259				project.provide("faucetUrl", FAUCET_URL)
   260				return
   261			}
   262			console.log("[e2e-setup] Starting anvil at", ANVIL_URL, "...")
   263			anvilProcess = spawn(
   264				ANVIL_BIN,
   265				["--host", "127.0.0.1", "--port", String(ANVIL_PORT), "--chain-id", "31337", "--slots-in-an-epoch", "1", "--silent"],
   266				{
   267					stdio: "pipe",
   268					detached: true,
   269				},
   270			)
   271			weStartedAnvil = true
   272	
   273			anvilProcess.stderr?.on("data", (data: Buffer) => {
   274				const line = data.toString().trim()
   275				if (line.includes("error") || line.includes("Error") || line.includes("address already in use")) {
   276					console.error("[anvil]", line.slice(0, 200))
   277				}
   278			})
   279			anvilProcess.once("exit", (code) => {
   280				if (weStartedAnvil && code !== 0 && code !== null) {
   281					console.error(`[anvil] exited unexpectedly with code ${code}`)
   282				}
   283			})
   284	
   285			try {
   286				await waitForAnvil(ANVIL_URL, 30_000)
   287				console.log("[e2e-setup] Anvil is ready")
   288			} catch (error) {
   289				console.error("[e2e-setup] Failed to start anvil:", error)
   290				await killProcessGroup(anvilProcess, "anvil", weStartedAnvil)
   291				anvilProcess = null
   292				project.provide("aztecTestConfig", undefined)
   293				project.provide("playgroundUrl", PLAYGROUND_URL)
   294				project.provide("faucetUrl", FAUCET_URL)
   295				return
   296			}
   297		}
   298	
   299		// ── Aztec (L2) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   300		const nodeAlreadyRunning = await checkNodeHealth(LOCAL_NODE_URL)
   301	
   302		if (nodeAlreadyRunning) {
   303			console.log("[e2e-setup] Local Aztec node already running at", LOCAL_NODE_URL)
   304			weStartedNode = false
   305		} else {
   306			console.log("[e2e-setup] Starting local Aztec network at", LOCAL_NODE_URL, "...")
   307			if (!fs.existsSync(AZTEC_BIN)) {
   308				// See comment above the matching ANVIL_BIN gate for the rationale.
   309				if (process.env.E2E_REQUIRE_SETUP === "1") {
   310					throw new Error(
   311						`[e2e-setup] FATAL: aztec CLI not found at ${AZTEC_BIN} and E2E_REQUIRE_SETUP=1 is set. ` +
   312							`Aborting run to prevent silent pass-by-skip. Ensure setup-aztec installed Aztec CLI ` +
   313							`AND created the ~/.aztec/current symlink (CI: see .github/actions/setup-aztec/action.yml).`,
   314					)
   315				}
   316				console.warn("[e2e-setup] aztec CLI not found at", AZTEC_BIN, "— skipping network setup")
   317				project.provide("aztecTestConfig", undefined)
   318				project.provide("playgroundUrl", PLAYGROUND_URL)
   319				project.provide("faucetUrl", FAUCET_URL)
   320				return
   321			}
   322	
   323			// Mandatory --data-directory per agent: aztec writes to $HOME/.aztec/data
   324			// by default for some subsystems, which would corrupt LMDB if two
   325			// agents run concurrently with the default path.
   326			fs.mkdirSync(AZTEC_DATA_DIR, { recursive: true })
   327	
   328			nodeProcess = spawn(
   329				AZTEC_BIN,
   330				[
   331					"start",
   332					"--local-network",
   333					"--port",
   334					String(AZTEC_PORT),
   335					"--admin-port",
   336					String(AZTEC_ADMIN_PORT),
   337					"--p2p.p2pPort",
   338					String(AZTEC_P2P_PORT),
   339					"--l1-rpc-urls",
   340					ANVIL_URL,
   341					"--data-directory",
   342					AZTEC_DATA_DIR,
   343					"--disable-admin-api-key",
   344				],
   345				{
   346					stdio: "pipe",
   347					detached: true,
   348					env: {
   349						...process.env,
   350						SEQ_MIN_TX_PER_BLOCK: "0",
   351						ETHEREUM_HOSTS: ANVIL_URL,
   352						ANVIL_PORT: String(ANVIL_PORT),
   353						AZTEC_PORT: String(AZTEC_PORT),
   354					},
   355				},
   356			)
   357			weStartedNode = true
   358	
   359			nodeProcess.stdout?.on("data", (data: Buffer) => {
   360				const line = data.toString().trim()
   361				if (line.includes("Aztec") || line.includes("ready") || line.includes("error")) {
   362					console.log("[aztec-node]", line.slice(0, 200))
   363				}
   364			})
   365			nodeProcess.stderr?.on("data", (data: Buffer) => {
   366				const line = data.toString().trim()
   367				if (line.includes("error") || line.includes("Error")) {
   368					console.error("[aztec-node]", line.slice(0, 200))
   369				}
   370			})
   371	
   372			try {
   373				await waitForLocalNode(LOCAL_NODE_URL, 90_000)
   374				console.log("[e2e-setup] Local Aztec node is ready")
   375			} catch (error) {
   376				console.error("[e2e-setup] Failed to start local node:", error)
   377				await killProcessGroup(nodeProcess, "aztec", weStartedNode)
   378				nodeProcess = null
   379				await killProcessGroup(anvilProcess, "anvil", weStartedAnvil)
   380				anvilProcess = null
   381				project.provide("aztecTestConfig", undefined)
   382				project.provide("playgroundUrl", PLAYGROUND_URL)
   383				project.provide("faucetUrl", FAUCET_URL)
   384				return
   385			}
   386		}
   387	
   388		// ── Playground dev server ──────────────────────────────────────────
   389		const playgroundAlreadyRunning = await probeHttp(PLAYGROUND_URL, 1500)
   390		if (playgroundAlreadyRunning) {
   391			console.log("[e2e-setup] Playground already running at", PLAYGROUND_URL)
   392			weStartedPlayground = false
   393		} else {
   394			console.log("[e2e-setup] Starting playground dev server at", PLAYGROUND_URL, "...")
   395			try {
   396				playgroundProcess = spawn("bun", ["run", "dev"], {
   397					cwd: PLAYGROUND_DIR,
   398					stdio: "pipe",
   399					detached: true,
   400					env: {
   401						...process.env,
   402						NODE_ENV: "test",
   403						VITE_DISABLE_HMR: "1",
   404						PLAYGROUND_PORT: String(PLAYGROUND_PORT),
   405					},
   406				})
   407				weStartedPlayground = true
   408	
   409				playgroundProcess.stdout?.on("data", (data: Buffer) => {
   410					const line = data.toString().trim()
   411					if (line.includes("Local:") || line.includes("error")) {
   412						console.log("[playground]", line.slice(0, 200))
   413					}
   414				})
   415				playgroundProcess.stderr?.on("data", (data: Buffer) => {
   416					const line = data.toString().trim()
   417					if (line.includes("error") || line.includes("Error")) {
   418						console.error("[playground]", line.slice(0, 200))
   419					}
   420				})
   421	
   422				await waitForHttp(PLAYGROUND_URL, 30_000)
   423				console.log("[e2e-setup] Playground is ready")
   424			} catch (error) {
   425				console.warn("[e2e-setup] Failed to start playground:", error)
   426				await killProcessGroup(playgroundProcess, "playground", weStartedPlayground)
   427				playgroundProcess = null
   428				// Continue without playground — tests that depend on it will skip / fail individually
   429			}
   430		}
   431		project.provide("playgroundUrl", PLAYGROUND_URL)
   432	
   433		// ── Faucet dev server (opt-in via FAUCET_DEV_PORT) ─────────────────
   434		// Only spawned when the test runner pre-allocated a faucet port. This
   435		// keeps the default network suite lightweight — faucet startup adds ~5s
   436		// + a Vite + Vue process per worktree.
   437		if (FAUCET_PORT && FAUCET_URL) {
   438			const faucetAlreadyRunning = await probeHttp(FAUCET_URL, 1500)
   439			if (faucetAlreadyRunning) {
   440				console.log("[e2e-setup] Faucet already running at", FAUCET_URL)
   441				weStartedFaucet = false
   442			} else {
   443				console.log("[e2e-setup] Starting faucet dev server at", FAUCET_URL, "...")
   444				try {
   445					faucetProcess = spawn("bun", ["run", "dev"], {
   446						cwd: FAUCET_DIR,
   447						stdio: "pipe",
   448						detached: true,
   449						env: {
   450							...process.env,
   451							NODE_ENV: "test",
   452							FAUCET_DEV_PORT: String(FAUCET_PORT),
   453						},
   454					})
   455					weStartedFaucet = true
   456	
   457					faucetProcess.stdout?.on("data", (data: Buffer) => {
   458						const line = data.toString().trim()
   459						if (line.includes("Local:") || line.includes("error")) {
   460							console.log("[faucet]", line.slice(0, 200))
   461						}
   462					})
   463					faucetProcess.stderr?.on("data", (data: Buffer) => {
   464						const line = data.toString().trim()
   465						if (line.includes("error") || line.includes("Error")) {
   466							console.error("[faucet]", line.slice(0, 200))
   467						}
   468					})
   469	
   470					await waitForHttp(FAUCET_URL, 30_000)
   471					console.log("[e2e-setup] Faucet is ready")
   472				} catch (error) {
   473					console.warn("[e2e-setup] Failed to start faucet:", error)
   474					await killProcessGroup(faucetProcess, "faucet", weStartedFaucet)
   475					faucetProcess = null
   476					// Continue — only faucet-specific tests will fail.
   477				}
   478			}
   479		}
   480		project.provide("faucetUrl", FAUCET_URL)
   481	
   482		await deployContractsAndProvide(project)
   483	}
   484	
   485	/**
   486	 * Deploy SponsoredFPC + a test Token, write `.test-config.json`, and write
   487	 * the ownership lock with PIDs + L1 contract addresses + the address book.
   488	 * On reuse the lock's `deployedConfig` lets us recreate `.test-config.json`
   489	 * without redeploying.
   490	 */
   491	async function deployContractsAndProvide(project: TestProject): Promise<void> {
   492		const existingLock = readLock()
   493		if (existingLock?.deployedConfig?.nodeUrl === LOCAL_NODE_URL) {
   494			fs.writeFileSync(CONFIG_PATH, JSON.stringify(existingLock.deployedConfig, null, 2))
   495			project.provide("aztecTestConfig", existingLock.deployedConfig)
   496			console.log("[e2e-setup] reused deployed contracts from lockfile:", existingLock.deployedConfig)
   497			return
   498		}
   499	
   500		let l1ContractAddresses: Record<string, string> | undefined
   501		let config: AztecTestConfig | undefined
   502		try {
   503			console.log("[e2e-setup] Deploying test contracts...")
   504			const { wallet, accounts, node, cleanup } = await createTestWallet(LOCAL_NODE_URL)
   505			try {
   506				const nodeInfo = await node.getNodeInfo()
   507				l1ContractAddresses = serializeL1ContractAddresses(nodeInfo.l1ContractAddresses)
   508				const minterAddress = accounts[0]
   509				const { paymentMethod, address: sponsoredFpcAddress } = await createSponsoredFeeOptions(wallet)
   510				const feeOptions = { paymentMethod }
   511	
   512				const tokenAddress = await deployTestToken(wallet, minterAddress, feeOptions)
   513	
   514				config = {
   515					nodeUrl: LOCAL_NODE_URL,
   516					tokenAddress,
   517					sponsoredFpcAddress,
   518					minterAddress: minterAddress.toString(),
   519				}
   520	
   521				fs.writeFileSync(CONFIG_PATH, JSON.stringify(config, null, 2))
   522				console.log("[e2e-setup] Test contracts deployed:", JSON.stringify(config, null, 2))
   523			} finally {
   524				await cleanup()
   525			}
   526			project.provide("aztecTestConfig", config)
   527		} catch (error) {
   528			console.error("[e2e-setup] Failed to deploy test contracts:", error)
   529			project.provide("aztecTestConfig", undefined)
   530			// Env-gated fail-loud. The `bun run e2e:agent` wrapper
   531			// (`scripts/e2e/agent.sh`) sets `E2E_REQUIRE_SETUP=1` to mark this
   532			// as a real test invocation where the sandbox is supposed to be
   533			// available. In that mode we propagate the deploy failure so vitest
   534			// exits non-zero with a clear message — instead of every test
   535			// gating on `describe.skipIf(!hasAztecTestConfig)` and silently
   536			// passing-by-skip. Without this gate, the suite was reporting

   579	function serializeL1ContractAddresses(addrs: unknown): Record<string, string> {
   580		if (!addrs || typeof addrs !== "object") return {}
   581		const out: Record<string, string> = {}
   582		for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(addrs as Record<string, unknown>)) {
   583			if (v == null) continue
   584			// AztecAddress / EthAddress instances expose `.toString()`; primitives
   585			// stringify naturally. Anything else gets serialized as JSON.
   586			const s = typeof v === "object" && "toString" in v ? String(v) : JSON.stringify(v)
   587			out[k] = s
   588		}
   589		return out
   590	}

   595	 * lockfile recorded. A foreign aztec on the same port reports different
   596	 * addresses and is rejected.

   598	async function verifyIdentity(url: string, expected: Record<string, string> | undefined): Promise<boolean> {
   599		if (!expected || Object.keys(expected).length === 0) return false
   600		try {
   601			const { createAztecNodeClient } = await import("@aztec/aztec.js/node")
   602			const node = createAztecNodeClient(url)
   603			const info = await node.getNodeInfo()
   604			const got = serializeL1ContractAddresses(info.l1ContractAddresses)
   605			for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(expected)) {
   606				if (got[k] !== v) {
   607					console.warn(`[e2e-setup] identity mismatch on ${k}: lock=${v} actual=${got[k] ?? "<missing>"}`)
   608					return false
   609				}
   610			}
   611			return true
   612		} catch (err) {
   613			console.warn("[e2e-setup] identity check failed:", err)
   614			return false
   615		}

   630		nodeProcess = null

   632		anvilProcess = null

   646	/**
   647	 * Send SIGTERM to the process group, wait up to 5s for clean exit, then
   648	 * SIGKILL escalate. Synchronous best-effort fallback for the `process.on("exit")`
   649	 * path lives in `bestEffortKill` below.
   650	 */
   651	async function killProcessGroup(child: ChildProcess | null, label: string, weStarted: boolean): Promise<void> {
   652		if (!child?.pid || !weStarted) return
   653		console.log(`[e2e-setup] Stopping ${label} (pid=${child.pid})...`)
   654		try {
   655			process.kill(-child.pid, "SIGTERM")
   656		} catch {
   657			try {
   658				child.kill("SIGTERM")
   659			} catch {
   660				// ignore
   661			}
   662		}
   663		const start = Date.now()
   664		while (child.exitCode === null && !child.killed && Date.now() - start < 5_000) {
   665			await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 100))
   666		}
   667		if (child.exitCode === null && !child.killed) {
   668			console.warn(`[e2e-setup] ${label} did not exit on SIGTERM; sending SIGKILL`)
   669			try {
   670				process.kill(-child.pid, "SIGKILL")
   671			} catch {
   672				try {
   673					child.kill("SIGKILL")
   674				} catch {
   675					// ignore
   676				}
   677			}
   678		}
   679	}
   680	
   681	/** Best-effort sync kill for the `process.on("exit")` path. Sync-only:
   682	 *  fires SIGTERM and lets the OS finish what it can — async waits aren't
   683	 *  available here. */
   684	function bestEffortKill(child: ChildProcess | null, weStarted: boolean): void {
   685		if (!child?.pid || !weStarted) return
   686		try {
   687			process.kill(-child.pid, "SIGTERM")
   688		} catch {
   689			try {
   690				child.kill("SIGTERM")
   691			} catch {
   692				// ignore
   693			}
   694		}
   695	}
   696	
   697	const onExit = () => {
   698		bestEffortKill(playgroundProcess, weStartedPlayground)
   699		bestEffortKill(nodeProcess, weStartedNode)
   700		bestEffortKill(anvilProcess, weStartedAnvil)
   701		clearLock()
   702	}
   703	process.on("SIGINT", onExit)
   704	process.on("SIGTERM", onExit)
   705	process.on("exit", onExit)

   716			faucetUrl?: string

   111		public async cancelJob(jobId: string): Promise<void> {

   113			// is in a pre-submit stage and cancel is meaningful — abort the
   114			// in-flight controller so the prove pipeline unwinds.

   120			// natural `succeeded` or `failed` terminal — preserving consistency
   121			// between journal stage and on-chain state.

    78	/** Navigate to a settings sub-page by URL segments. Only the first segment
    79	 *  has a `setting-nav-<segment>` testid on the index page; deeper segments
    80	 *  must be exposed by their parent page (add one when the test needs it).
    81	 *  Example: `navigateToSettings(page, "accounts")`. */
    82	export async function navigateToSettings(page: Page, ...segments: string[]): Promise<void> {
    83		await clickNavTab(page, "settings")
    84		await page.waitForFunction(() => window.location.hash === "#/popup/settings", { timeout: 5_000 })
    85	
    86		const pathSoFar: string[] = []
    87		for (const segment of segments) {
    88			pathSoFar.push(segment)
    89			const href = `#/popup/settings/${pathSoFar.join("/")}`
    90			// First segment: use the testid on the settings index. Deeper
    91			// segments: fall back to the SettingItem's `to` prop since child
    92			// pages don't yet have a consistent testid naming convention.
    93			const testidSelector = `[data-testid="setting-nav-${pathSoFar.join("-")}"]`
    94			const clicked = await page.evaluate(
    95				({ id, hash }: { id: string; hash: string }) => {
    96					const byTestId = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>(id)
    97					if (byTestId) {
    98						byTestId.click()
    99						return "testid"
   100					}
   101					const a = [...document.querySelectorAll("a")].find(
   102						(el) => el.getAttribute("href") === hash || el.getAttribute("to") === hash.slice(1),
   103					)
   104					if (a) {
   105						a.click()
   106						return "href"
   107					}
   108					// Final fallback: router-link renders `<a>` with no href, but Vue Router
   109					// listens on 'to'. Dispatch a synthetic click on the element whose
   110					// textContent matches our segment title — this is the weakest path.
   111					return null
   112				},
   113				{ id: testidSelector, hash: href },
   114			)
   115	
   116			if (!clicked) {
   117				throw new Error(`navigateToSettings: no setting nav target for ${href} (expected testid ${testidSelector})`)
   118			}
   119	
   120			await page.waitForFunction((expected: string) => window.location.hash.startsWith(expected), { timeout: 5_000 }, href)
   121			// No explicit post-route sleep — every caller follows with its own
   122			// `waitForSelector` for an element on the landed page, which gives a
   123			// deterministic mount signal. The previous fixed 200ms padding was
   124			// wasted on every fast path. Confirmed safe across 26 smoke call
   125			// sites + 6 network sites in Phase 3 audit.
   126		}
   127	}
   128	
   129	// ── Network ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   130	
   131	/**
   132	 * Switch to a network by name. The header chip now routes to the Manage
   133	 * Networks settings page; from there we drill into the network's detail
   134	 * page and tap "Set as active".
   135	 */
   136	export async function switchToNetwork(page: Page, networkName: string): Promise<void> {
   137		// Snapshot the BEFORE state. The header text identifies the chain the
   138		// popup is currently on; the activeAccount key identifies the address
   139		// `setupActiveAccount` last wrote. Both are needed to disambiguate
   140		// "this is a real chain switch" vs "this is a no-op repeat switch":
   141		//   - real switch  → activeAccount FLIPS to the target chain's address
   142		//                    (different secret-derivation key per chain)
   143		//   - repeat switch → activeAccount stays put; the network watcher fires
   144		//                    but `setupActiveAccount` re-picks the same account
   145		const beforeHeader = await page.evaluate(() => {
   146			const btn = document.querySelector('[data-testid="network-button"]')
   147			return (btn?.textContent ?? "").trim()
   148		})
   149		const beforeAccount = await page.evaluate(async () => {
   150			const r = await chrome.storage.local.get("nulo:ui:activeAccount")
   151			return (r["nulo:ui:activeAccount"] as string | undefined) ?? ""
   152		})
   153		// Exact match (not substring) on the trimmed header text. Substring
   154		// matching collides when a custom network is renamed to contain another
   155		// network's name (e.g., "Local Backup" would falsely look like a no-op
   156		// when switching to "Local"). Network names are user-visible identifiers,
   157		// so an exact match against the rendered header is the precise contract.
   158		const isRealSwitch = beforeHeader !== networkName
   159	
   160		// Navigate via the header chip → Manage Networks → detail page → set active.
   161		// SettingItem rows render as <a> elements whose `href` can be `null`; raw
   162		// `.click()` doesn't reliably fire on those, so the row tap uses a synthetic
   163		// dispatchEvent (matches openNetworkDetail's contract).
   164		await clickByTestId(page, "network-button")
   165		const rowSelector = `[data-testid="network-row"][data-network-name="${networkName}"]`
   166		await page.waitForSelector(rowSelector, { visible: true, timeout: 5_000 })
   167		await page.evaluate((sel: string) => {
   168			const row = document.querySelector(sel) as HTMLElement | null
   169			row?.dispatchEvent(new MouseEvent("click", { bubbles: true, cancelable: true }))
   170		}, rowSelector)
   171		await page.waitForSelector('[data-testid="network-set-active"]', { visible: true, timeout: 5_000 })
   172		await clickByTestId(page, "network-set-active")
   173		// Return to /popup/general so callers can keep using general-page selectors
   174		// (importToken, refreshBalances, gas-balance reads, …). The chip flow took
   175		// us from general → settings list → detail; navigate explicitly back rather
   176		// than `history.go(-2)`, which is fragile under deep-link bypasses.
   177		await page.evaluate(() => {
   178			window.location.hash = "/popup/general"
   179		})
   180		await page.waitForFunction(() => window.location.hash.includes("/popup/general"), { timeout: 5_000 })
   181	
   182		// First: wait for the network-button header to display the target name
   183		// exactly. This is the "appStore.network changed" signal.
   184		await page.waitForFunction(
   185			(target: string) => {
   186				const btn = document.querySelector('[data-testid="network-button"]')
   187				return !!btn && (btn.textContent ?? "").trim() === target
   188			},
   189			{ timeout: 30_000, polling: 250 },
   190			networkName,
   191		)
   192	
   193		// Then: wait for the network watcher's `setupActiveAccount` to land. On
   194		// a real switch, `nulo:ui:activeAccount` flips away from `beforeAccount`
   195		// because each chain derives its own address. On a repeat switch we just
   196		// confirm the existing value is still set (the watcher may briefly clear
   197		// the `account` ref while re-fetching).
   198		await page.waitForFunction(
   199			async ({ prev, real }: { prev: string; real: boolean }) => {
   200				const r = await chrome.storage.local.get("nulo:ui:activeAccount")
   201				const addr = r["nulo:ui:activeAccount"]
   202				if (typeof addr !== "string" || addr.length === 0) return false
   203				return real ? addr !== prev : true
   204			},
   205			{ timeout: 30_000, polling: 250 },
   206			{ prev: beforeAccount, real: isRealSwitch },
   207		)
   208	}
   209	
   210	/** Switch to the Local Network (chain ID 0, http://localhost:8080). */
   211	export async function switchToLocalNetwork(page: Page): Promise<void> {
   212		await switchToNetwork(page, "Local Network")
   213	}

    55	export interface TryCreateQueuedJournalDeps {
    56		journal: OperationJournalService
    57		profile: ProfileService
    58		dappSession: DappSessionService
    59		networkSvc: NetworkService
    60		logger: ILogger
    61	}
    62	
    63	/**
    64	 * Create a journal record at `queued` stage so the activity feed surfaces
    65	 * an incoming sendTx the moment it arrives — BEFORE the per-session FIFO
    66	 * lets the handler open the approval popup.
    67	 *
    68	 * Returns the new record's id, or `undefined` on any failure. Best-effort
    69	 * visibility: a failure here NEVER blocks the actual handler from running
    70	 * (the handler falls back to creating its own in-flight record via
    71	 * `beginDappExecuteJournal`).
    72	 *
    73	 * Cheap pre-auth gates: skip queued visibility when there's no active
    74	 * profile, no dapp session, or no sendTx capability grant. Avoids
    75	 * surfacing requests that the handler will reject anyway.
    76	 *
    77	 * Cap enforcement is atomic: the count-then-create section runs under
    78	 * `queuedCreationLock` so concurrent arrivals can't all see a stale
    79	 * "below cap" count and over-create.
    80	 */
    81	export async function tryCreateQueuedJournal(
    82		message: WalletMessage,
    83		session: ActiveSession,
    84		deps: TryCreateQueuedJournalDeps,
    85	): Promise<string | undefined> {
    86		const { journal, profile, dappSession, networkSvc, logger } = deps
    87		try {
    88			const activeProfile = await profile.getActiveProfile()
    89			if (!activeProfile) return undefined
    90	
    91			const chainId = chainInfoToChainId(session)
    92			const dapp = await dappSession.tryGetDappSessionByOriginAndChain(session.origin, String(chainId))
    93			if (!dapp?.accounts?.length) return undefined
    94	
    95			// sendTx requires the `transaction` capability (the capability type
    96			// scoped to send-like operations). Pre-auth-gate skip when missing.
    97			const hasSendTxGrant = (dapp.capabilityGrants ?? []).some((g) => g.capability.type === "transaction")
    98			if (!hasSendTxGrant) return undefined
    99	
   100			// DappSession.accounts is string[] of CAIP. Parse to get the bare address.
   101			const firstCaipAccount = dapp.accounts[0] as CaipAccount
   102			const { address: accountAddress } = parseCaipAccount(firstCaipAccount)
   103	
   104			// `networkId` for activity-feed scoping must be the INTERNAL network row id
   105			// (RecentActivityView.journalRecordInScope filters on `network.id`), NOT
   106			// `String(chainId)`. Without this resolution the queued card never renders.
   107			const network = await resolveNetworkByChainId(networkSvc, chainId)
   108			if (!network) return undefined
   109	
   110			// Critical section: cap check + record create must be atomic.
   111			await queuedCreationLock.enter()
   112			try {
   113				const sessionQueuedCount = await journal.countOperations({
   114					sessionId: session.sessionId,
   115					stage: "queued",
   116				})
   117				if (sessionQueuedCount >= MAX_QUEUED_PER_SESSION) {
   118					logger.log(
   119						"wallet-sdk-bg",
   120						LogLevel.Debug,
   121						`Per-session queued cap reached for ${session.sessionId}; skipping queued visibility`,
   122					)
   123					return undefined
   124				}
   125				const globalQueuedCount = await journal.countOperations({ stage: "queued" })
   126				if (globalQueuedCount >= MAX_QUEUED_GLOBAL) {
   127					logger.log("wallet-sdk-bg", LogLevel.Warn, `Global queued cap reached (${MAX_QUEUED_GLOBAL}); skipping queued visibility`)
   128					return undefined
   129				}
   130	
   131				const primaryMethod = extractPrimaryMethodFromSendTx(message)
   132				// Chip label: prefer the dApp's display name from its stored
   133				// session metadata (DappSession.dappMetadata.name, set at
   134				// discover/verify time). Falls back to "Unknown dapp" to match
   135				// the pre-existing execution path (`dapp-interaction/service.ts:309`)
   136				// so the queued record's subtitle equals what the live-claim record
   137				// would have gotten — keeps the chip text identical across queued
   138				// vs first-tx paths. NOTE: dappMetadata lives on DappSession (our
   139				// stored session), NOT on ActiveSession (the wallet-sdk transport
   140				// session) — those are two different types that both happen to be
   141				// in scope here. Previously this used `session.origin` (the full
   142				// URL on the transport session), which surfaced raw URLs in the
   143				// activity-card chip.
   144				const dappName = dapp.dappMetadata?.name ?? "Unknown dapp"
   145				const record = await journal.createOperation({
   146					kind: "dapp_execute",
   147					origin: "dapp",
   148					profileId: activeProfile.id,
   149					sessionId: session.sessionId,
   150					accountAddress,
   151					networkId: network.id,
   152					title: primaryMethod ?? "Transaction",
   153					subtitle: dappName,
   154					initialStage: { stage: "queued" },
   155				})
   156				return record.id
   157			} finally {
   158				queuedCreationLock.leave()
   159			}
   160		} catch (error) {
   161			logger.log("wallet-sdk-bg", LogLevel.Warn, `tryCreateQueuedJournal failed: ${getErrorMessage(error)}`)
   162			return undefined
   163		}
   164	}
   165	
   166	/**
   167	 * Best-effort primary-method extraction from a sendTx wallet message.
   168	 * Mirrors what `executeAztecSendTx` does to compute the title at journal
   169	 * creation time, so the title is consistent between the queued surface
   170	 * and the post-claim in-flight surface.
   171	 */
   172	export function extractPrimaryMethodFromSendTx(message: WalletMessage): string | undefined {
   173		if (message.type !== "sendTx") return undefined
   174		const args = message.args as unknown[] | undefined
   175		if (!Array.isArray(args)) return undefined
   176		const exec = args[0] as { calls?: Array<{ name?: string }> } | undefined
   177		return pickPrimaryMethod(exec?.calls)
   178	}

The `self` contract value for public execution contexts.\n\nuse crate::{\n    context::{calls::{PublicCall, PublicStaticCall}, PublicContext},\n    event::{event_emission::emit_event_in_public, event_interface::EventInterface},\n};\nuse crate::protocol::{address::AztecAddress, traits::{Deserialize, Serialize}};\n\n/// Core interface for interacting with aztec-nr contract features in public execution contexts.\n///\n/// This struct is automatically injected into every [`external`](crate::macros::functions::external) and\n/// [`internal`](crate::macros::functions::internal) contract function marked with `\"public\"` by the Aztec macro\n/// system and is accessible through the `self` variable.\n///\n/// ## Type Parameters\n///\n/// - `Storage`: The contract's storage struct (defined with [`storage`](crate::macros::storage::storage), or `()` if\n/// the contract has no storage\n/// - `CallSelf`: Macro-generated type for calling contract's own non-view functions\n/// - `CallSelfStatic`: Macro-generated type for calling contract's own view functions\n/// - `CallInternal`: Macro-generated type for calling internal functions\npub struct ContractSelfPublic<Storage, CallSelf, CallSelfStatic, CallInternal> {\n    /// The address of this contract\n    pub address: AztecAddress,\n\n    /// The contract's storage instance, representing the struct to which the\n    /// [`storage`](crate::macros::storage::storage) macro was applied in your contract. If the contract has no\n    /// storage, the type of this will be `()`.\n    ///\n    /// This storage instance is specialized for the current execution context (public) and\n    /// provides access to the contract's state variables.\n    ///\n    /// ## Developer Note\n    ///\n    /// If you've arrived here while trying to access your contract's storage while the `Storage` generic type is set\n    /// to unit type `()`, it means you haven't yet defined a Storage struct using the\n    /// [`storage`](crate::macros::storage::storage) macro in your contract. For guidance on setting this up, please\n    /// refer to our docs: https://docs.aztec.network/developers/docs/guides/smart_contracts/storage\n    pub storage: Storage,\n\n    /// The public execution context.\n    pub context: PublicContext,\n\n    /// Provides type-safe methods for calling this contract's own non-view functions.\n    ///\n    /// Example API:\n    /// ```noir\n    /// self.call_self.some_public_function(args)\n    /// ```\n    pub call_self: CallSelf,\n\n    /// Provides type-safe methods for calling this contract's own view functions.\n    ///\n    /// Example API:\n    /// ```noir\n    /// self.call_self_static.some_view_function(args)\n    /// ```\n    pub call_self_static: CallSelfStatic,\n\n    /// Provides type-safe methods for calling internal functions.\n    ///\n    /// Example API:\n    /// ```noir\n    /// self.internal.some_internal_function(args)\n    /// ```\n    pub internal: CallInternal,\n}\n\nimpl<Storage, CallSelf, CallSelfStatic, CallInternal> ContractSelfPublic<Storage, CallSelf, CallSelfStatic, CallInternal> {\n    /// Creates a new `ContractSelfPublic` instance for a public function.\n    ///\n    /// This constructor is called automatically by the macro system and should not be called directly.\n    pub fn new(\n        context: PublicContext,\n        storage: Storage,\n        call_self: CallSelf,\n        call_self_static: CallSelfStatic,\n        internal: CallInternal,\n    ) -> Self {\n        Self { context, storage, address: context.this_address(), call_self, call_self_static, internal }\n    }\n\n    /// The address of the contract address that made this function call.\n    ///\n    /// This is similar to Solidity's `msg.sender` value.\n    ///\n    /// ## Incognito Calls\n    ///\n    /// Contracts can call public functions from private ones hiding their identity (see\n    ///\n    /// [`ContractSelfPrivate::enqueue_incognito`](crate::contract_self::ContractSelfPrivate::enqueue_incognito)).\n    /// This function reverts when executed in such a context.\n    ///\n    /// If you need to handle these cases, use [`PublicContext::maybe_msg_sender`].\n    pub fn msg_sender(self: Self) -> AztecAddress {\n        self.context.maybe_msg_sender().unwrap()\n    }\n\n    /// Emits an event publicly.\n    ///\n    /// Public events are emitted as plaintext and are therefore visible to everyone. This is is the same as Solidity\n    /// events on EVM chains.\n    ///\n    /// Unlike private events, they don't require delivery of an event message.\n    ///\n    /// # Example\n    /// ```noir\n    /// #[event]\n    /// struct Update { value: Field }\n    ///\n    /// #[external(\"public\")]\n    /// fn publish_update(value: Field) {\n    ///     self.emit(Update { value });\n    /// }\n    /// ```\n    ///\n    /// # Cost\n    ///\n    /// Public event emission is achieved by emitting public transaction logs. A total of `N+1` fields are emitted,\n    /// where `N` is the serialization length of the event.\n    pub fn emit<Event>(&mut self, event: Event)\n    where\n        Event: EventInterface + Serialize,\n    {\n        emit_event_in_public(self.context, event);\n    }\n\n    /// Makes a public contract call.\n    ///\n    /// Will revert if the called function reverts or runs out of gas.\n    ///\n    /// # Arguments\n    /// * `call` - The object representing the public function to invoke.\n    ///\n    /// # Returns\n    /// * `T` - Whatever data the called function has returned.\n    ///\n    /// # Example\n    /// ```noir\n    /// self.call(Token::at(address).transfer_in_public(recipient, amount));\n    /// ```\n    ///\n    pub unconstrained fn call<let M: u32, let N: u32, T>(self, call: PublicCall<M, N, T>) -> T\n    where\n        T: Deserialize,\n    {\n        call.call(self.context)\n    }\n\n    /// Makes a public read-only contract call.\n    ///\n    /// This is similar to Solidity's `staticcall`. The called function cannot modify state or emit events. Any nested\n    /// calls are constrained to also be static calls.\n    ///\n    /// Will revert if the called function reverts or runs out of gas.\n    ///\n    /// # Arguments\n    /// * `call` - The object representing the read-only public function to invoke.\n    ///\n    /// # Returns\n    /// * `T` - Whatever data the called function has returned.\n    ///\n    /// # Example\n    /// ```noir\n    /// self.view(Token::at(address).balance_of_public(recipient));\n    /// ```\n    ///\n    pub unconstrained fn view<let M: u32, let N: u32, T>(self, call: PublicStaticCall<M, N, T>) -> T\n    where\n        T: Deserialize,\n    {\n        call.view(self.context)\n    }\n}\n"

The `self` contract value for public execution contexts.\n\nuse crate::{\n    context::{calls::{PublicCall, PublicStaticCall}, PublicContext},\n    event::{event_emission::emit_event_in_public, event_interface::EventInterface},\n};\nuse crate::protocol::{address::AztecAddress, traits::{Deserialize, Serialize}};\n\n/// Core interface for interacting with aztec-nr contract features in public execution contexts.\n///\n/// This struct is automatically injected into every [`external`](crate::macros::functions::external) and\n/// [`internal`](crate::macros::functions::internal) contract function marked with `\"public\"` by the Aztec macro\n/// system and is accessible through the `self` variable.\n///\n/// ## Type Parameters\n///\n/// - `Storage`: The contract's storage struct (defined with [`storage`](crate::macros::storage::storage), or `()` if\n/// the contract has no storage\n/// - `CallSelf`: Macro-generated type for calling contract's own non-view functions\n/// - `CallSelfStatic`: Macro-generated type for calling contract's own view functions\n/// - `CallInternal`: Macro-generated type for calling internal functions\npub struct ContractSelfPublic<Storage, CallSelf, CallSelfStatic, CallInternal> {\n    /// The address of this contract\n    pub address: AztecAddress,\n\n    /// The contract's storage instance, representing the struct to which the\n    /// [`storage`](crate::macros::storage::storage) macro was applied in your contract. If the contract has no\n    /// storage, the type of this will be `()`.\n    ///\n    /// This storage instance is specialized for the current execution context (public) and\n    /// provides access to the contract's state variables.\n    ///\n    /// ## Developer Note\n    ///\n    /// If you've arrived here while trying to access your contract's storage while the `Storage` generic type is set\n    /// to unit type `()`, it means you haven't yet defined a Storage struct using the\n    /// [`storage`](crate::macros::storage::storage) macro in your contract. For guidance on setting this up, please\n    /// refer to our docs: https://docs.aztec.network/developers/docs/guides/smart_contracts/storage\n    pub storage: Storage,\n\n    /// The public execution context.\n    pub context: PublicContext,\n\n    /// Provides type-safe methods for calling this contract's own non-view functions.\n    ///\n    /// Example API:\n    /// ```noir\n    /// self.call_self.some_public_function(args)\n    /// ```\n    pub call_self: CallSelf,\n\n    /// Provides type-safe methods for calling this contract's own view functions.\n    ///\n    /// Example API:\n    /// ```noir\n    /// self.call_self_static.some_view_function(args)\n    /// ```\n    pub call_self_static: CallSelfStatic,\n\n    /// Provides type-safe methods for calling internal functions.\n    ///\n    /// Example API:\n    /// ```noir\n    /// self.internal.some_internal_function(args)\n    /// ```\n    pub internal: CallInternal,\n}\n\nimpl<Storage, CallSelf, CallSelfStatic, CallInternal> ContractSelfPublic<Storage, CallSelf, CallSelfStatic, CallInternal> {\n    /// Creates a new `ContractSelfPublic` instance for a public function.\n    ///\n    /// This constructor is called automatically by the macro system and should not be called directly.\n    pub fn new(\n        context: PublicContext,\n        storage: Storage,\n        call_self: CallSelf,\n        call_self_static: CallSelfStatic,\n        internal: CallInternal,\n    ) -> Self {\n        Self { context, storage, address: context.this_address(), call_self, call_self_static, internal }\n    }\n\n    /// The address of the contract address that made this function call.\n    ///\n    /// This is similar to Solidity's `msg.sender` value.\n    ///\n    /// ## Incognito Calls\n    ///\n    /// Contracts can call public functions from private ones hiding their identity (see\n    ///\n    /// [`ContractSelfPrivate::enqueue_incognito`](crate::contract_self::ContractSelfPrivate::enqueue_incognito)).\n    /// This function reverts when executed in such a context.\n    ///\n    /// If you need to handle these cases, use [`PublicContext::maybe_msg_sender`].\n    pub fn msg_sender(self: Self) -> AztecAddress {\n        self.context.maybe_msg_sender().unwrap()\n    }\n\n    /// Emits an event publicly.\n    ///\n    /// Public events are emitted as plaintext and are therefore visible to everyone. This is is the same as Solidity\n    /// events on EVM chains.\n    ///\n    /// Unlike private events, they don't require delivery of an event message.\n    ///\n    /// # Example\n    /// ```noir\n    /// #[event]\n    /// struct Update { value: Field }\n    ///\n    /// #[external(\"public\")]\n    /// fn publish_update(value: Field) {\n    ///     self.emit(Update { value });\n    /// }\n    /// ```\n    ///\n    /// # Cost\n    ///\n    /// Public event emission is achieved by emitting public transaction logs. A total of `N+1` fields are emitted,\n    /// where `N` is the serialization length of the event.\n    pub fn emit<Event>(&mut self, event: Event)\n    where\n        Event: EventInterface + Serialize,\n    {\n        emit_event_in_public(self.context, event);\n    }\n\n    /// Makes a public contract call.\n    ///\n    /// Will revert if the called function reverts or runs out of gas.\n    ///\n    /// # Arguments\n    /// * `call` - The object representing the public function to invoke.\n    ///\n    /// # Returns\n    /// * `T` - Whatever data the called function has returned.\n    ///\n    /// # Example\n    /// ```noir\n    /// self.call(Token::at(address).transfer_in_public(recipient, amount));\n    /// ```\n    ///\n    pub unconstrained fn call<let M: u32, let N: u32, T>(self, call: PublicCall<M, N, T>) -> T\n    where\n        T: Deserialize,\n    {\n        call.call(self.context)\n    }\n\n    /// Makes a public read-only contract call.\n    ///\n    /// This is similar to Solidity's `staticcall`. The called function cannot modify state or emit events. Any nested\n    /// calls are constrained to also be static calls.\n    ///\n    /// Will revert if the called function reverts or runs out of gas.\n    ///\n    /// # Arguments\n    /// * `call` - The object representing the read-only public function to invoke.\n    ///\n    /// # Returns\n    /// * `T` - Whatever data the called function has returned.\n    ///\n    /// # Example\n    /// ```noir\n    /// self.view(Token::at(address).balance_of_public(recipient));\n    /// ```\n    ///\n    pub unconstrained fn view<let M: u32, let N: u32, T>(self, call: PublicStaticCall<M, N, T>) -> T\n    where\n        T: Deserialize,\n    {\n        call.view(self.context)\n    }\n}\n"

node_modules/@defi-wonderland/aztec-standards/target/vault_contract-Vault.json:433:      "source": "pub mod test;\n\nuse aztec::macros::aztec;\n\n#[aztec]\npub contract Vault {\n    use aztec::{\n        authwit::auth::{\n            assert_current_call_valid_authwit, assert_current_call_valid_authwit_public,\n        },\n        context::PrivateContext,\n        macros::{functions::{external, initializer, internal, only_self, view}, storage::storage},\n        protocol::address::AztecAddress,\n        state_vars::PublicImmutable,\n    };\n    use token_contract::Token;\n\n    // Rounding direction that the vault uses to calculate shares and assets\n    global ROUND_DOWN: bool = false;\n    global ROUND_UP: bool = true;\n\n    // Maximum value for a u128 (2**128 - 1)\n    global MAX_U128_VALUE: u128 = 340282366920938463463374607431768211455;\n\n    /// @param admin The address with permission to set the shares token (one-time setup)\n    /// @param asset The underlying asset token address\n    /// @param shares The shares token address (minter must be this vault)\n    /// @param vault_offset The offset used to prevent inflation attacks\n    #[storage]\n    struct Storage<Context> {\n        admin: PublicImmutable<AztecAddress, Context>,\n        asset: PublicImmutable<AztecAddress, Context>,\n        shares: PublicImmutable<AztecAddress, Context>,\n        vault_offset: PublicImmutable<u128, Context>,\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Initializes the vault with asset, offset, and configuration\n    /// @dev The admin must call set_shares() after deploying the shares token with this vault as minter.\n    ///      The vault address can be precomputed before shares exists since shares is not a constructor arg.\n    ///      This 2-step deployment exists because contract instance publishing is private-only, so a public\n    ///      factory cannot deploy and wire both contracts atomically. Once public instance registration is\n    ///      supported, this can be simplified to a single-step deployment.\n    ///      See: https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/issues/20771\n    /// @param admin The address with permission to set the shares token (one-time setup)\n    /// @param asset The underlying asset token address\n    /// @param vault_offset The offset used to prevent inflation attacks (typically 1)\n    #[external(\"public\")]\n    #[initializer]\n    fn constructor(admin: AztecAddress, asset: AztecAddress, vault_offset: u128) {\n        assert(vault_offset > 0, \"vault_offset must be greater than 0\");\n        self.storage.admin.initialize(admin);\n        self.storage.asset.initialize(asset);\n        self.storage.vault_offset.initialize(vault_offset);\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Sets the shares token address (one-time, admin-only, immutable after set)\n    /// @dev Must be called after deploying the shares token with this vault as minter.\n    ///      PublicImmutable.initialize() ensures this can only ever be set once -- any subsequent\n    ///      call will revert. All vault operations read shares via PublicImmutable.read() which\n    ///      reverts if shares has not been initialized, so the vault is inoperable until this is called.\n    /// @param shares The shares token address (minter must be this vault)\n    #[external(\"public\")]\n    fn set_shares_token(shares: AztecAddress) {\n        let admin = self.storage.admin.read();\n        assert(self.msg_sender().eq(admin), \"caller is not admin\");\n        self.storage.shares.initialize(shares);\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Sets the shares token and makes an initial deposit for inflation-attack protection\n    /// @dev Must be called after deploying the shares token with this vault as minter.\n    ///      PublicImmutable.initialize() ensures this can only ever be set once -- any subsequent\n    ///      call will revert. All vault operations read shares via PublicImmutable.read() which\n    ///      reverts if shares has not been initialized, so the vault is inoperable until this is called.\n    /// @param shares The shares token address (minter must be this vault)\n    /// @param initial_deposit The initial deposit amount of the asset\n    /// @param depositor The address of the initial depositor of the assets\n    /// @param nonce The nonce used for authwitness for the transfer of the initial deposit\n    #[external(\"public\")]\n    fn set_shares_token_with_initial_deposit(\n        shares: AztecAddress,\n        initial_deposit: u128,\n        depositor: AztecAddress,\n        nonce: Field,\n    ) {\n        let admin = self.storage.admin.read();\n        assert(self.msg_sender().eq(admin), \"caller is not admin\");\n        self.storage.shares.initialize(shares);\n\n        // Caller deposits assets, shares are minted to this contract and are permanently locked.\n        let from = depositor;\n        let to = self.address;\n\n        // Assets could be donated to the vault's precomputed address before deployment, but such assets are\n        // ignored at this point to ensure the asset<>share conversion is 1:1 for the initial deposit.\n        let total_assets: u128 = 0;\n        let total_supply: u128 = 0;\n        let vault_offset = self.storage.vault_offset.read();\n\n        // Calculate shares to mint for the initial deposit.\n        let deposit_shares = _convert_to_shares(\n            initial_deposit,\n            total_assets,\n            total_supply,\n            vault_offset,\n            ROUND_DOWN,\n        );\n\n        // Transfer the assets from the sender to the vault\n        let asset_token = self.storage.asset.read();\n        self.call(Token::at(asset_token).transfer_public_to_public(from, to, initial_deposit, nonce));\n\n        // Mint shares to this contract address (permanently locked)\n        self.call(Token::at(shares).mint_to_public(to, deposit_shares));\n    }\n\n    /** ==========================================================\n     * ========================= DEPOSIT =========================\n     * ======================================================== */\n\n    // ## Note on ARC-403 assets\n    // ARC-403 defines a single authorization hook (`authorize_private` / `authorize_public`) that fires\n    // on the source side BEFORE a transfer - there is no recipient-side hook.\n    // Users can therefore use the hook to reenter the vault when the asset token calls `authorize` before\n    // moving balances in deposit, withdraw, issue, and redeem functions.\n    //\n    // To keep the contract safe, reentrancy should not happen at half-updated states:\n    //  - Assets should be transferred into the vault BEFORE minting shares. Reentrancy would only happen before any\n    //    balance is updated.\n    //  - Assets should be transferred out of the vault AFTER burning shares. Reentrancy would only happen after all\n    //    balances are updated.\n\n    /// @notice Deposits the underlying asset from a public balance and receives shares to a public balance\n    /// @param from The address of the sender\n    /// @param to The address of the recipient\n    /// @param assets The amount of assets to deposit\n    /// @param nonce The nonce used for authwitness\n    #[external(\"public\")]\n    fn deposit_public_to_public(from: AztecAddress, to: AztecAddress, assets: u128, nonce: Field) {\n        let asset_token = self.storage.asset.read();\n        let shares_token = self.storage.shares.read();\n        self.internal._validate_from_public(from);\n\n        // Calculate shares to mint\n        let total_assets = self.internal._total_assets();\n        let total_supply = self.internal._total_supply_of_shares();\n        let vault_offset = self.storage.vault_offset.read();\n        let shares =\n            _convert_to_shares(assets, total_assets, total_supply, vault_offset, ROUND_DOWN);\n        assert(shares > 0, \"Zero shares, insufficient assets\");\n\n        // Order matters: transfer before minting to neutralize ARC-403 reentrancy.\n        // Take the assets from the sender\n        self.call(Token::at(asset_token).transfer_public_to_public(\n            from,\n            self.address,\n            assets,\n            nonce,\n        ));\n\n        // Mint shares to the recipient\n        self.call(Token::at(shares_token).mint_to_public(to, shares));\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Deposits the underlying asset from a public balance and receives shares to a private balance\n    /// @dev The shares are calculated based on the ratio (total_supply + offset) / (total_assets + 1) minus any acceptable slippage.\n    ///      The ratio can only decrease or remain the same as time goes by. Any asset excess is kept by the contract as yield.\n    /// @param from The address of the sender\n    /// @param to The address of the recipient\n    /// @param assets The amount of assets to deposit\n    /// @param shares The amount of shares that should be minted to the recipient\n    /// @param nonce The nonce used for authwitness\n    #[external(\"private\")]\n    fn deposit_public_to_private(\n        from: AztecAddress,\n        to: AztecAddress,\n        assets: u128,\n        shares: u128,\n        nonce: Field,\n    ) {\n        let shares_token = self.storage.shares.read();\n        _validate_from_private::<5>(self.context, from);\n\n        // Validate in public that `assets` is sufficient for the requested shares\n        // Order matters: enqueue settlement first so asset transfer executes before shares total_supply increase\n        self.enqueue_self.settle_deposit_public_to_private_internal(from, assets, shares, nonce);\n\n        // Mint shares to the recipient's private balance\n        self.call(Token::at(shares_token).mint_to_private(to, shares));\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Deposits the underlying asset from a private balance and receives shares to a private balance\n    /// @dev The shares are calculated based on the ratio (total_supply + offset) / (total_assets + 1) minus any acceptable slippage.\n    ///      The ratio can only decrease or remain the same as time goes by. Any asset excess is kept by the contract as yield.\n    /// @param from The address of the sender\n    /// @param to The address of the recipient\n    /// @param assets The amount of assets to deposit\n    /// @param shares The amount of shares that should be minted to the recipient\n    /// @param nonce The nonce used for authwitness\n    #[external(\"private\")]\n    fn deposit_private_to_private(\n        from: AztecAddress,\n        to: AztecAddress,\n        assets: u128,\n        shares: u128,\n        nonce: Field,\n    ) {\n        let asset_token = self.storage.asset.read();\n        let shares_token = self.storage.shares.read();\n        _validate_from_private::<5>(self.context, from);\n\n        // Order matters: transfer before minting to neutralize ARC-403 reentrancy.\n        // Take the assets from the sender\n        self.call(Token::at(asset_token).transfer_private_to_public(\n            from,\n            self.address,\n            assets,\n            nonce,\n        ));\n\n        // Mint shares to the recipient's private balance\n        self.call(Token::at(shares_token).mint_to_private(to, shares));\n\n        // Validate in public that `assets` is sufficient for the requested shares\n        self.enqueue_self.settle_deposit_private_to_private_internal(assets, shares);\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Deposits the underlying asset from a private balance and receives shares to a public balance\n    /// @param from The address of the sender\n    /// @param to The address of the recipient\n    /// @param assets The amount of assets to deposit\n    /// @param nonce The nonce used for authwitness\n    #[external(\"private\")]\n    fn deposit_private_to_public(from: AztecAddress, to: AztecAddress, assets: u128, nonce: Field) {\n        let asset_token = self.storage.asset.read();\n        _validate_from_private::<4>(self.context, from);\n\n        // Order matters: transfer before minting to neutralize ARC-403 reentrancy.\n        // Take the assets from the sender\n        self.call(Token::at(asset_token).transfer_private_to_public(\n            from,\n            self.address,\n            assets,\n            nonce,\n        ));\n\n        // Calculate and mint shares to the recipient in public\n        self.enqueue_self.settle_deposit_private_to_public_internal(to, assets);\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Deposits the underlying asset from a public balance and receives shares to a private balance\n    /// @dev min_shares is the amount of shares that will be minted immediately in private.\n    ///      Any additional shares the recipient is entitled to, will be minted through a commitment once the call is executed publicly.\n    ///      This additional amount can only be known at public execution.\n    /// @param from The address of the sender\n    /// @param to The address of the recipient\n    /// @param assets The amount of assets to deposit\n    /// @param min_shares The amount of shares that should be minted to the recipient in private\n    /// @param nonce The nonce used for authwitness\n    #[external(\"private\")]\n    fn deposit_public_to_private_exact(\n        from: AztecAddress,\n        to: AztecAddress,\n        assets: u128,\n        min_shares: u128,\n        nonce: Field,\n    ) {\n        let shares_token = self.storage.shares.read();\n        _validate_from_private::<5>(self.context, from);\n\n        // Initialize commitment on the shares token that allows to mint outstanding shares to the recipient in public\n        let partial_note =\n            self.call(Token::at(shares_token).initialize_transfer_commitment(to, self.address));\n\n        // Mint any outstanding shares without revealing the recipient and updates the shares total supply\n        // Reverts if min_shares is greater than allowed\n        // Order matters: enqueue settlement first so asset transfer executes before shares total_supply increase\n        self.enqueue_self.settle_deposit_public_to_private_exact_internal(\n            from,\n            partial_note,\n            assets,\n            min_shares,\n            nonce,\n        );\n\n        // Mint min_shares to the recipient's private balance\n        self.call(Token::at(shares_token).mint_to_private(to, min_shares));\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Deposits the underlying asset from a private balance and receives shares to a private balance\n    /// @dev min_shares is the amount of shares that will be minted immediately in private.\n    ///      Any additional shares the recipient is entitled to, will be minted through a commitment once the call is executed publicly.\n    ///      This additional amount can only be known at public execution.\n    /// @param from The address of the sender\n    /// @param to The address of the recipient\n    /// @param assets The amount of assets to deposit\n    /// @param min_shares The amount of shares that should be minted to the recipient in private\n    /// @param nonce The nonce used for authwitness\n    #[external(\"private\")]\n    fn deposit_private_to_private_exact(\n        from: AztecAddress,\n        to: AztecAddress,\n        assets: u128,\n        min_shares: u128,\n        nonce: Field,\n    ) {\n        let asset_token = self.storage.asset.read();\n        let shares_token = self.storage.shares.read();\n
